[Note: Picks up immediately after the House of Chains prologue]
In the dying realm of Kurald Emurlahn, the elder goddess Kilmandaros walks past six dead dragons
[Note: that she probably killed]
Ghosts are attracted to the dragons’ blood and gets trapped in it for eternity
Kilmandaros was a pale skinned extremely large creature with long, multi jointed arms that almost scraped the floor. Her fists were cracked and bloody from the killing
Three dragons fly and disappear above her
The pools of dragon blood harden into sheets, lifted up to form walls, then sank and fell into other realms depending on the blood’s aspect
Starvald Demelain, blood of dragons and death of blood
Kurald Emurlahn is in civil war, foreigners come to scavenge and take their own piece of the realm
[Note: Shattered pieces of Kurald Emurlahn]
Kilmandaros comes to a rent that was a crevasse in the hills, carved out by a giant claw. A tear in space that bled power
She walks through it into the mortal realm
Gothos finishes up using Omtose Phellack to seal the aftermath of Edur and Andii vs. K'Chain Che'Malle
Emo Jaghut thoughts, feels naive to think there used to be omniscient caring god
Gothos walks up a hill that suddenly descends into a large crevasse/chasm
Uses Omtose Phellack to slow his descent into the chasm where he meets with Mael and Kilmandaros
Aftermath of Kilmandaros crushing and breaking the eleint form of Scabandari Bloodeye’s wings and legs. Scabandari lays dying
Kilmandaros wants to kill Scabandari and return to Kurald Emurlahn
Her children in the [mortal realm] lost their way
[Note: What other people have extra joints?]
She tried to save Kurald Emurlahn because other realms might shatter the same way. It was a mistake to try to
Gothos’ Omtose Phellack Ritual to preserve the land is the reason why Kilandaros shouldn't kill Scabandari
If Scabandari dies while in the Ritual, his soul would be released
Gothos uses a “cryptically unspecified item” as the Finnest to capture Scabandari’s soul the moment Kilmandaros crushes Scabandari’s skull to kill him
Gothos keeps the Finnest with Scabandari’s soul instead of handing it over to Mael. Doesn't know what to do with it yet

Gothos is Icarium’s dad. He is the Guardian of Tremorlor, the Azath House on Seven Cities. Icarium’s mind broke when he tried to free his father from imprisonment, ignorant that his father actually liked the solitude and quiet life. He is the
author of Gothos’ Folly quoted throughout the series that has bits and pieces of knowledge about the races and world.
Gothos also has a brother, Gethol, who was formerly the Herald of High House Death. In Memories of Ice, Gethol

presented Hood’s offer to save the Grey Swords from the Tenescowri but was rejected after insulting Fener for his impending fall. Falling out of favor with Hood, the Crippled God recruited Gethol as Herald of his yet to be High House
Chains. Gethol later recruited Kallor as King of High House Chains. In Bonehunters, Gethol offered to restore Tene
Baralta’s scars (because Tene was a vain person) for a favor with Empress Laseen, which never came to fruition because Lostara Yil killed Tene Baralta.

cards.h: *** Lether has no Hold of Death

i.html: Because of Gothos’s Omtose Phellack Ritual preserving the land, he inadvertently closed the paths of the dead. This resulted in Lether being prone to wraiths, ghosts, and undead. It’s one of the reasons why the Tiste Edur had the Tiste Andii wraiths (whom the Edur betrayed in the war) as their servants.
Once the Omtose Phellack sorcery thawed and the Azath Tower died, the Hold of Death manifested once again on the continent.
Kilmandaros returns to the rent leading to Kurald Emurlahn, Anomandaris Purake is there
Rake offers to help Kilmandaros because Edgewalker is busy elsewhere
Rake knows betrayal is never worth it, unlike Scabandari
Soletaken and feral dragons are warring in Kurald Emurlahn
Kilmandaros was told by Mael that Osserc would try to stop Rake from killing Scabandari to avenge his brother, Silchas Ruin
Rake didn't bother because he knew Kilmandaros and Mael were enough to take care of Scabandari
Doesn't pity Silchas Ruin for being imprisoned in the Azath, as it will inevitably end. Jokingly envies the isolation
Kilmandaros accepts Rake’s help to expel ‘pretenders’, let Kurald Emurlahn die on its own, and keep the Throne of Shadow unoccupied
They enter the rent and start working
Atri-Preda Bivatt of the Drene Garrison traveled 21 days to investigate the western coasts of the Bluerose Sea
Event occurs during the last days of Ezgara Diskanar’s reign, near the end of Midnight Tides
This part of the ocean was violent enough to destroy a Meckros City about 80 years ago
200 soldiers of the Tattered Banner Army, 30 Bluerose light cavalry, and 400 support staff
Letur Anict, a merchant and “Factor” of Drene that accompanied the expedition
Bivatt doesn't trust him
About 4,000 to 5,000 war canoes were on the shore. If they each carried 100 people, almost half a million total people
However, there was no trace of them. An entire population had arrived on the continent and Bivatt has no idea where they are
Bivatt orders Letur Anict to have his mages study the canoes, while Bivatt planned to have Ceda Kuru Qan’s acolyte students to report what Letur Anict would omit from his reports
Redmask woke up to wolves mournful howling and traveled to the aftermath of a battle on a hill between Drene soldiers and a foreign people he didn't recognize
Drene carried their dead with them, only their enemies were left behind
The defeated faction wore grey and black uniforms. Painted sigils on the armor were a pair of wolf heads. One white furred and one eye. The other with silver and black fur
Pale skin, blonde or red hair, blue or grey eyes, and many of them were women
Foreigners. None were of the empire either Letherii nor Bluerose, or from the border territories of the Awl, D’rhasilhani, Keryn, Bolkando, or Saphinaud
Normally the dun furred wolves of the Awl’dan region wouldn't go near humans, especially strange that the wolves had come and only ate the hearts
No other scavenger animals touched the corpses either
Redmask had two dread companions that killed for pleasure, were indifferent to human sentiments
Book One:
The Emperor in Gold
“Invigilator” Karos Invictad, commander of the Patriotists, Lether’s police force
Wears red leather silks, wields a staff made of black Edur blackwood with silver caps studded in onyx
Tanal Yathvanar, Karos’ assistant, gives him a puzzle made by Senorbo of Bluerose
Karos has a puzzle hobby
Karos and Tanal go to the prison compound to meet with Bruthen Trana (Den-Ratha tribe, Tiste Edur), liaison to the Tiste Edur
Presents 18 of the ~320 Letherii inmates. Half of them are unconscious from lack of food and water
The prisoners have no actual crimes charged against them, just suspicions and associations with parties the police don't like
A man apart of “dissenting elements” at the physician’s college
A poet that proudly calls for revolution
A tavern keeper whose customers are undesirables and disenchanted soldiers
About 1/3 are scheduled for Drownings, no one survives anymore because the weights are too heavy
Bruthen Trana silently leaves
Karos and Tanal return to their office, Karos quickly solves the Senorbos puzzle
Discussion on Karos’ 45% interest in the Inn of the Belly up Snake
Plan a meeting with the master of the Liberty Consign
Wants to look into why they have little money despite their takings
Karos wants to investigate Bruthen Trana to find out why he visits the prison weekly
Rautos Hivanar is the head of the wealthy Hivanar family, as well as the master of the Liberty Consign, an organization of Lether’s wealthiest families
Venitt Sathad’s (his servant) family has been Indebted to the Hivanar house for six generations
Rautos suspects someone is economically sabotaging Lether
However, Rautos is more interested in ancient constructs and artifacts revealed from floodwaters off the riverbank of the Hivanar estate
The soil and plants of the river bottom had been washed away to reveal cobbled streets of arranged boulders framed in wooden posts
Bronze and copper artifacts that did not seem to function as any sort of stone or food tool
One bronze item had a flange, was long and roundish, bent at right angles, cross hatch pattern around the elbow, neither end attached to anything. Was not a piece of a larger mechanism
One thin circular copper sheet with uniform holes in no particular pattern
Karos Invictad sends a messenger regarding the sabotager
Rautos plans to send Venitt to Drene, Letur Anict’s reports have been unsatisfactory
Rautos looks out at the main docks and sees the Esterrict merchant trader vessel whose flag looks burnt
“Atri-Preda” Bivatt’s Bluerose cavalry massacres an Awl camp
[Note: Atri-Preda is the equivalent of a Fist of a town or territory. Not to be confused with Preda, like a High Fist]
Brohl Handar (Arapay tribe, Tiste Edur) is the new “Overseer” (governor) of Drene placed two weeks ago. He watches with discomfort as the Letherii army dismantles the camp
Heads were scalped for the gold jewelry in Awl braids
Many Awl had colorful tattoos, they’re skinned and placed on shields for decoration
Less than 100 Tiste Edur were in this remote region of Rhulad’s empire. Brohl Handar used to be a chief of a clan that hunted seals, feels disillusioned and wondered wtf he is even doing here
Brohl is confused by Letherii culture and asks Bivatt to clarify some things
Letur Anict (Bivatt’s boss) calls the Awl people trespassers, Bivatt makes it clear they are not. This was fought for wealth and greed

Brohl realizes the Edur conquest of the Letherii Empire (in response to the Letherii attempt at subjugating the Edur as they had with the Nerek, Faraed, and Tarthenal tribes) was ultimately an economic war
The Letherii convinced its people with the lie that the Awl were part of a coalition among the D’rhasilhani, Ak’ryn, Bolkando, and Saphinaud that threatened Lether’s eastern border
Truth is that no alliance exists, the Awl were already in decline. These wars are to make Letur Anict richer
Brohl realizes the Edur loves wealth as much as the Letherii do. Several Hiroth tribe members enjoy estates, lands, and hundreds of Indebted slaves back in Drene
Seren Pedac, Fear Sengar, Udinaas, Kettle, and Silchas Ruin are being pursued by the Tiste Edur
Udinaas and Kettle were captured, tortured, and raped by enslavers after getting caught stealing from a farm
Silchas Ruin walked right up to the slavers, demanded they be unchained, and wields his two long swords that makes high pitched noises like music when he swings
Slits the throat of the lead Tiste Edur who thought Silchas Ruin was kin
One Edur gets slashed in the chest
A second Edur has a ⅓ of his head sliced off, picks up the pieces of his head, and drunkenly walks for the rest of the time
A third Edur has his leg cut off and yells at the Letherii to fight
With his left hand Silchas parries a sword, flicks his wrist to disarm, then pierce a fourth Edur’s chest
With his right hand Silchas feints high then pierces the fifth Edur’s eye into the brain
Cuts down two Letherii, the remaining 8 Letherii flee
Udinaas grapples the worst Letherii that raped Kettle and strangles him with his chains
Silchas Ruin veers into eleint form and slaughters the remaining Letherii slavers
Udinaas wants to free the rest of the slaves, the alternative to kill them to ensure their silence
Fear recognized the Edur as the Merude tribe. Searched the leader for the keys and admits unwillingness to murder his kin
Fear thought the better option was to buy Udinaas and Kettle back to spare the bloodshed
Seren Pedac is indifferent to Silchas killing fellow Letherii humans
Udinaas believes Fear is upset that he's lost his leadership role, especially to a Tiste Andii
Fear still believes the lie that Silchas Ruin betrayed Scabandari [Note: The truth is the other way around]
Seren Pedac thinks that Rhulad is still scared of his brother, having the warlocks set magical traps in both Letheras and the wild lands of the east
The group decides to sneak around the fort ahead of them, Wyval has been gone for a month and can't scout ahead for them
[Possible Spoilers: The Wyval straight up just left and never appears in the series again]
The slaver wagon is full of weapons and armor

Acquitor, a sanctioned liaison between the Letherii Empire and the northern tribes. She guided Buruk the Pale and Hull Beddict to the meet with the Warlock King, Hannan Mosag. Before the meeting, she helped Buruk’s Nerek servants by asking Mayen to give them her blessing (this inadvertently consecrated the ground to their goddess, the Eres’al, which later protected them from Letherrii sorcery). Buruk was Indebted, blackmailed by Queen Janall Diskanar to further her plans to subjugate the Tiste Edur. Hull Beddict wanted to fight on the Tiste Edur side against the Letherii Empire who subjugated the Faraed, Nerek, and Tarthenal peoples that he grew to love.

The meeting gets complicated as Rhulad returns wielding the mottled sword and declares himself the new Emperor of the Tiste Edur. Seren Pedac and Buruk return to Trate, where Buruk commits suicide out of guilt. The Letherii assaulted Trate on their way to Edur territory and soldiers had raped Seren while she was drunk and depressed. She gets rescued by Iron Bars and the Crimson Guard to escape into Kurald Galain.

In Kurald Galain, Seren Pedac was able to strike a bargain with Sandalath Drukorlat to help guide them in exchange for delivering her ring to her body so that Drukorlat can escape her limbo. Seren escorted the Crimson Guard to Letheras, the mage Corlo helped Seren harness her control over Mockra which she didn’t know she had, as well as carry out a ritual to release the grief and guilt she’s bottled up.

In Letheras, Seren declines the offer to join the Crimson Guard. Later, the Errant had nudged Trull and Fear Sengar to find Seren to guide Fear to escape Lether and find Scabandari’s soul to return Father Shadow to the Tiste Edur. Meanwhile, Trull immediately falls in love and lays a sword at her door, an Edur marriage proposal.
Later, Silchas Ruin arrives with Kettle, Udinaas, and Wither as Iron Bars had recommended Seren to also help them flee Letheras

The eldest Sengar brother. Their mother, Uruth Sengar, was upset that the Warlock King for relying on demons rather than Kurald Emurlahn. She sent her children to the Stone Bowl, where they found Scabandari’s shattered eleint skull and confront the truth that their Father Shadow was dead, his soul trapped elsewhere. The Sengar brothers were also sent on the Warlock King’s mission to retrieve the Crippled God’s sword, which ended up possessing the youngest brother Rhulad. Rhulad was cursed with immortality and forced his way to become the leader of the Tiste Edur. Fear led the Tiste Edur into several battles all the way to Letheras, forgiving all the crimes his youngest brother had done including raping and impregnating his wife Mayen.

When Brys Beddict defeated Rhulad in the throne room, Fear Sengar fled and was nudged by the Errant to seek out Seren Pedac as his guide to find Scabandari’s soul to return Father Shadow and save the Tiste Edur.

Udinaas was an Indebted Letherii working in Trate, when the Tiste Edur invaded the city and enslaved him. Udinaas ended up serving the house of Sengar. In an attempt for freedom, Feather Witch attempted to summon a Wyval servant to Silchas Ruin, but instead the Wyval infected Udinass with its blood. Ever since, Udinaas had been having fever dreams including encountering Menandore, a goddess hated by the Tiste Edur, who raped him. A Tiste Andii wraith, Wither, approaches Udinaas to help get revenge on the Edur and hide the presence of the Wyval. In another dream, Udinaas found himself in an Imass Refugium where he met Rud Elalle, Udinaas’ son from Menandore’s rape.

Udinaas travels with the Edur on their conquest of the Letherii Empire. When they reached Letheras, Wyval took over and transformed Udinaas’s body, slaughtering Jheck and Edur on the way to the Azath Tower to free the Wyval’s master Silchas Ruin. Wither presents himself as Killanthir, a High Mage under Silchas Ruin during the wars against the KCCM. The Wyval destroys Udinaas’s broken body, Wither convinces Kettle to give him a drop of blood to save Udinaas. Wither drags Udinaas’ body as he, Kettle, and Silchas Ruin find Seren Pedac to escape the city.

Kettle is an undead girl that was the guardian of the dying Azath Tower. She would kill people and feed them to the Azath to keep it alive. Kettle ended up helping Silchas Ruin try to escape to deal with the other dangerous creatures trapped inside. Over the course of the events, she befriends lots of people including Tehol, Bugg, Brys, Ceda Kuru Qan, Shurq Elalle, etc.

Kettle’s memories slowly returned and she slowly regained life. She had the soul of a Forkrul Assail and of a Nameless One priestess who had been preparing Kettle’s body since birth to use as her vessel. Kettle was also considered a true child of the Eres. After Silchas Ruin was freed, she helped Wither give Udinaas a drop of her blood to save his life and joined their party to Seren Pedac’s house to flee Letheras.

An albino Tiste Andii, brother to Anomander Rake and Andarist. Silchas Ruin led several thousand Tiste Andii to leave the civil wars of Kurald Galain and find a new home in the mortal world. As Scabandari led the Tiste Edur to flee Kurald Emurlahn as it was shattering, they joined forces to fight the K’Chain Che’Malle and settle a new life in this world. In the end, Scabandari backstabbed Silchas Ruin and imprisoned him in the Azath Tower.
The Tiste Andii that survived Scabandari’s betrayal fled to the Bluerose mountains where they founded the Bluerose Kingdom.

As the Azath Tower was dying, it made a deal with Silchas Ruin so that he would remain to destroy the most dangerous creatures that was imprisoned in it including the Seregahl with assistance from the Crimson Guard. Iron Bars told them they could ask Seren Pedac to help them escape. Thus Silchas Ruin, Kettle, Wither (formerly a Tiste Andii high mage), and Kettle joined Seren Pedac.
Tanal Yathvanar rapes and torturs a woman that was sentenced to a Drowning
Had idolized Gerun Eberict who was a ‘noble killer’ that murdered thousands under the pretense of cleansing the streets. Wants to avenge him one day

[Note: Gerun Eberict was Finadd (Captain) of the Letherii Palace Guard. He thwarted an assassination attempt on King Diskanar that he orchestrated himself to earn him the King’s Leave which granted him immunity to commit any crimes against anyone excluding the royal family. With the immunity, he’s killed up to 7,000 people. Enraged after Tehol carried out a plan to ransack Eberict’s estate, he kills a Nerek woman, Urusan, who begged him for coin. Eberict was on his way to kill Tehol during the Edur invasion of Lether when he caught Mayen (Rhulad’s wife) and planned to gang rape her with his men. Mayen killed herself, then Eberict is killed by Unn, a Nerek-Tarthenal, to avenge Urusan.]
Enters the office during a meeting between Karos Invictad and Rautos Hivanar
Rautos is unable to find the sabotage suspect because he leaves no trail, hoards coin depleting wealth from the economy
Scholars and academics of the Liberty Consign made appeals to their leader, Rautos, on behalf of their friends that have been targeted by the Patriotist police
Karos accepts the appeals and Rautos leaves
The woman Tanal just raped was a Liberty Consign scholar. Karos orders him to free her, revoke her punishment, and be financially responsible to pay restitutions to her family
Tanal worries about reprisal and is determined to make Karos suffer as much as he does
Tehol Beddict and Bugg have a silly conversation
Tries to balance “Ezgara the two-headed insect” on a fulcrum point
[Note: I’d imagine a random nail or splinter sticking out of the floor]
Ate a wax tablet
Tehol measured a drowned cat three years ago to make a joke at this moment
Bugg says extensions are needed for the x16 vaults that are more than halfway under the river
Each vault 3x2 man heights, all filled
Would drag down 3-4, unspecified
Tehol wants Bugg to build a box with no lid for ‘comeuppance’
Depravity holds a certain fascination… the sicker the soul, the sweeter it's comeuppance
Seren Pedac, Fear Sengar, Silchas Ruin, Udinaas, and Kettle are on a paved road, by the Jasp river, that leads into a moraine (dirt and rocks deposited by glaciers). Their side had lots of forests
The mountain on the other side of the trail was a stark contrast. Completely barren of nature, the mountain was one of the first K’Chain Che’Malle skykeeps
Windows carved facing outward, vulnerable to attacks. Newer sky keeps would face homes inwards for self defense
Silchas Ruin recalls this sky keep was destroyed by at least a dozen eleint unleashing Starvald Demelain
Wither appears, explains the KCCM tried to annihilate all existence which provoked the dragons’ response
Silchas Ruins warns Wither that the frozen blood can trap Wither and Silchas can't free him
Seren Pedac jokingly suggests traveling via Silchas Ruin’s soletaken form
Silchas has too much bloodlust and anger when he veers into a dragon
Seren Pedac mocks Silchas for obsessing and being vengeful over Scabandari who basically doesn't exist anymore
Silchas hints something more complex is going on, their future will be unexpected
The group climbs up the sky keep ruins, over the remnants of metopes, cornices, and friezes
Fear Sengar wants to stay on the path, but Udinass wants to take a door shaped cave
Udinaas mocks Fear for wanting to stay on the more treacherous icy path out of glory and walks into the cave himself
Silchas Ruin is amused of a slave mocking a Tiste Edur, rest of the group follow Udinaas
The cave leads into a corridor full of bats
Udinaas asks Seren Pedac about lighting the lantern for him, jokes how the Edur cared little for their slaves
The floor has a layer of guano
A prisoner with broken feet screams outrage against the Letherii Empire as he’s dragged across the courtyard

Karos Invictad says people with certainty in a black and white world [Note: simple and naive] are also the most vulnerable when their convictions are challenged, and can be slowly persuaded into most loyal allies

People who are skeptics, understand the world is grey, and that nothing is simple are greatest enemy of the Patriotist police. The greatest insult to them is to call them naive, assault them with derisive dismissal, certainty, and arrogance to strike fear in them
Karos personally has certainty only in one thing, power shapes the world
Karos has his officers identify the people who are swayed by the screaming man’s treasonous words, those he can sway to his side
The people who are silent are the ones that must die
Believes both extremes of the political spectrum are willing to spill blood to defend their reality, and have a hatred for skeptics and people that question
Karos sees the contempt Tanal Yathvanar has for him and mocks him for it
Tanal informs that Karos has received a puzzle from an unknown sender
Tanal Yathvanar descends the dungeons that have been recently flooded and drained into the chamber where he tortured and raped Janath Anar, senior lecturer at the Academy of Imperial Learning
She refutes any notion of moral relativism

‘The structures of s culture do not circumvent nor excuse self evident injustice or inequity. The status quo is not sacred, not an altar to paint in rivers of blood. Tradition and habit are not sound arguments.’
Tanal comes down with food and water, supposed to free her but her insults cut deep and he slaps her face and leaves her there
Overseer Brohl Handar is being escorted in his private carriage through the throngs of people of the marketplace and compares his old life to the new
Strange how the precious bloodwood is now used for mundane bowls and cups, or to trim an ostentatious carriage
Thinks about how even though the Edur conquered the Letherii, the Edur became victims of its capitalism
Comfort was like an intoxicating, but not fatal, poison. Thrives on inequality between the rich and the poor
Felt powerless as Drene’s Overseer against a hidden web of power defending their wealth
Felt his report of Letur Anict’s war against tribal peoples for personal wealth would be intercepted by Letur Anict’s connections including Chancellor Triban Gnol
The Liberty Consign might be the center of the web that Brohl is too small and far away to challenge
Through the blinds of his carriage Brohl watches an arrest at the gates. Both the Letherii officers and the person being detained were eerily silent
Though the detainee had no weapons, Brohl believes they will be charged for sedition anyways with some fabricated excuse, fascism
Orbyn Truthfinder, the fat despicable leader of the local Patriotist office, enters the carriage
Brohl openly believes the Patriotist has non-existent conspiracies, Orbyn says the Bolkando Conspiracy is led by the Liberty Consign which the Patriotists gets paid to help with
Orbyn reports sightings of Silchas Ruin’s party heading east towards the mountains
Hannan Mosag had predicted Silchas Ruin’s path, but is not urgent because the paths are blocked
Orbyn leaves, alarm bells are ringing and Brohl has his driver head to them
Drene used to be a city-state that warred with the Awl and accepted Letherii aid to defeat the Awl
The occupying Letherii troops in Drene never left, Drene’s king and royal family were killed
Decades later, it was revealed that the Drene-Awl conflict itself was orchestrated by the Letherii. Revealed too late for anyone to care
Redmask hides in the shadows of the Drene garrison, follows two Patriotists in an alleyway, kills them and skins their faces

Wields a ‘cadaran whip’ that's studded with coin sized half-moon blades and a ‘rygtha crescent axe’ with two three-quarter blades perpendicular to each other (I’m guessing it’s a 4-sided axe that looks more like a flanged mace)
The trailing third Patriotist raises an alarm, a squad of x5 guards appears
Redmask kills two with his cadaran whip and chopped into the face of a third
Wraps the whip around to decapitate a fourth, crashes the axe into the fifth
Drops the whip, holds the axe at both ends and crushes the last Pariotist with the haft
More guards appear, Redmask charges towards them
Atri-Preda Bivatt (Drene military leader) arrives at the aftermath of Redmask’s massacre of the Patriotists and Drene city guards
About 27 bodies, only two are alive as another squad pursues Redmask
Orbyn Truthfinder (local Patriotist leader) appears, observes that Redmask’s exile from the tribes has ended
Overseer Brohl Handar appears
Atri-Preda Bivatt tries to dismiss herself as busy, Brohl demands explanations
Redmask is the brother of a girl kidnapped during a Drene-Awl conflict
To obtain the Awl’s herds, Letur Anict kidnapped the daughter of a clan leader to trade her for it
The Awl were known to kidnap Letherii children, thus was their justification to do the same
The daughter committed suicide by stabbing her heart, the Factor massacred the tribe anyways and took herds
Years later, the Factor would lose back-to-back against the Awl, led by lone survivor Redmask (before he got his redmask)
However, Redmask was unable to convince the Awl elders to unite the clans against the Letherii
Redmask spoke “unwise words” against the Awl elders and was exiled
Brohl wonders if it's the real clan leader son or an impostor, Bivatt confirms that Redmask is using the mythical Awl bladed whip and axe weapons
The cadaran whip and rygtha crescent axe were used against a non-human enemy to the east
The Awl lost the war and fled west towards Drene
Letherii expeditions to the east were unsuccessful, being wiped out at the border kingdoms
One survivor spoke of ‘the Hissing Night’, a voice of death, and became mad. She was untreatable and thus was put to death
Bivatt requests calling for Tiste Edur reinforcements if Redmask succeeds in unifying the Awl tribes
Brohl Handar feels its his chance to speak to Emperor Rhulad and Hannan Mosag
Redmask flees Drene, killing more Letherii riders that tried to chase after him
Redmask rides through old Awl lands, since his return from exile he only ever found destroyed and abandoned remnants of his people
Two K’Chain Che'Malle, Sag’Churok (male) and Gunth Mach (female), followed and protected him. Redmask doesn't know why

cards.h: Scene 10 (Skykeep in the Bluerose Mountains, Seren Pedac)

i.html: Seren Pedac and co. travel deeper into the skykeep in the Bluerose Mountains
Seren is fascinated by Silchas Ruin, how he seems near death-like and sane despite millenia of being buried
Fear tries to provoke Silchas, that the Edur women passed the truth of Scabandari betraying him, but still wonders who was the first traitor
Udinaas mocks Fear, asks why Rhulad hasn't sent a full force to kill Silchas
Kettle says it's because the Crippled God guiding Rhulad
The Crippled God isn't ready for open war yet and doesn't want them to travel eastward where there are secrets
Kettle gained this info from ghosts while she was in the Azath
A vast wheel is about to turn for the last time before it closes and reveal a truth to its maker
[Note: Speculating that this is Icarium]
Seren is frustrated by Kettle’s obscure words, but Silchas Ruin intends to heed them
‘The Liberty Consign of Merchants’. Merchant organization of Lether’s wealthiest families formed after the Edur conquest
Rautos Hivanar, leader and obsessed with artifacts being uncovered
Venitt Sathad, Indebted servant to Rautos
Letur Anict, “Factor” (spymaster) of Drene who’s sending false reports back to get rich off war against the Awl
‘The Patriotists’. Fascist, misogynistic, rapist police of the Letherii Empire
Karos Invictad, “Invigilator” (commander). Obsessed with puzzles
Tanal Yathvanar, personal bitch ass assistant
Orbyn Truthfinder, section commander in Drene
The Letherii Empire
Bivatt, “Atri-Preda” (Fist) of Drene
Brohl Handar, “Overseer” (Governor) of Drene, Tiste Edur
An expedition into the eastern wildlands by the Liberty Consign found a dying K’Chain Che’Malle in a crevice
Suffered wounds from the Awl’s cadaran bladed whip and the rygtha axe
Atri-Preda Pufanan Ibyris in the expedition kills the KCCM
[Note: thanks nakor87 for the correction!]
Nisall, First Concubine to the dead King Ezgara Diskanar, is now First Consort to Rhulad
Nisall saw Rhulad as a child. After sex, Rhulad would crawl on the floor like cripple to curl up in the corner of the room and weep
Nisal recalled the events after Brys had defeated Rhulad, died to the poison
Watched the [Guardian of the Names] pick up Brys and kill Rhulad, activating his death and revival, then leaves
Rhulad revives and crawls his way to discard Diskanar’s corpse and slumps onto the throne
Chancellor Triban Gnol immediately kneels before his new emperor
First Consort Turudal Brizad is nowhere to be found
Rhulad proclaims Hannan Mosag his Ceda, no longer a Warlock King and shrieks at him to drag Queen Janall and Prince Quillas’ mangled corpses away
Rhulad tells the whore to stay, Nisall yells at him
Rhulad apologize and genuinely offers that she can stay as First Concubine or leave without harm
Trull Sengar returns to the throne room and pleads Rhulad to drop the cursed sword
Rhulad orders for Trull to be Shorn
Nisall’s heart breaks as she watches Trull resign and toss away his weapons, sacrificing himself for his brother Fear
[Note: Events that happen between Midnight Tides and House of Chains]
Nisall chose to remain as First Concubine because she pitied Rhulad and for her own ambitions as Rhulad no longer had anyone to trust by his side
Back in the present, Rhulad whimpers in the corner, replaying the conversation in the throne room, begging Trull for forgiveness and to guide him with his honor
Nisall is impressed that after every night full of nightmares, Rhulad faces the petitions organized and the people of Lether presented to him
Nisall realizes through his judgments that Rhulad has an earnest, decent soul trying to do the best he can despite his trauma
Triban Gnol sees Nisall as a rival

King Ezgara Diskanar, a king who preferred to wear commoner’s modest wear than royal garb. Prepared himself to be Emperor of the First Empire reborn according to the prophecy of the Seventh Closure. Built the Eternal Domicile to be the new palace for the reborn empire
‘First Concubine’ Nisall, was on King Diskanar’s council
‘First Eunuch’ Nifadas, loyal advisor to the king that respected Hull Beddict
‘Ceda’ Kura Qan, high mage that liked Brys Beddict. Was killed by Hannan Mosag
Queen Janall Diskanar, manipulated the war between Lether and the Tiste Edur by sending Indebted to hunt seals, infringing on Edur territory
Prince Quillas, stupid and useless
‘Chancellor’ Triban Gnol, advisor that was responsible for the subjugation of the Nerek, Tarthenal, and Faraed tribes

‘First Consort’ Turudal Brizad, aka Errastas the Errant. A god whose power is to subtly influence people through nudges. Main objective was to stop the Jheck from reaching their D’ivers god, the Pack, who was imprisoned in the dying Azath Tower. Errastas also nudged Brys to drink the poisoned wine that killed him.
The Jaghut Ganath explained that the Errant was a god of change, ‘the enemy of ennui and stagnation’ and thus the enemy of the Forkrul Assail as well
The Jheck, descendants of the Beast Ritual on Seven Cities that survived the purge of the T’lan Imass by escaping to the Letheras continent
Bruthen Trana attempts to see Emperor Rhulad Sengar, but is repeatedly denied by Chancellor Triban Gnol
Bruthen suspects the chancellor of handpicking the petitioners and coaching them on what to say to Rhulad
Bruthen goes to the wing of the Eternal Domicile closest to the river, still damp despite the ingenious pylons that saved the palace from floods during Bugg’s construction
Walls were knocked down to let it air out the dampness
Bruthen Trana walks through one of the holes that led to the Azath Tower
Bruthen passes by gravestones of Fallen Champions that were able to kill Rhulad at least once, of note was a Tarthenal that had killed Rhulad seven times before being slain
[Note: thanks for nakor87 for the correction!]
Out of curiosity Bruthen reached down one of the urns and found the chalice cup that poisoned Brys Beddict
Bruthen Trana prays for Brys’ return
The Errant, is in the Cedance, the chamber in the Old Palace where Kuru Qan observed the Tiles
A narrow walkway suspended by chains, hanging knee high over Tiles arranged in spiral in the floor
The Errant considered this place his foundation of power as Master of the Tiles
The Errant feels fear as a pattern in the Tiles form out of his control, the Tiles have been blank since King Ezgara Diskanar and Ceda Kuru Qan died
Senses Chaos and a god’s meddling with the old and new pantheons
The carved tiles are currently blank. Not a single Hold would reveal
Wonders if Kuru Qan, the greatest Ceda since the First Empire, had cursed him beyond Qan’s death
Aware of [the Crippled God] manipulating the Tiste Edur and how his power comes from pain
The Errant reluctantly believes he'll have to ask help from Mael

The Errant is an Elder God and Master of the Tiles that had disguised himself as Turudal Brizad, the First Consort to the former Queen Janall (now deceased), whose persona existed in every generation of Letherii history. The Errant’s power is the nudge, like the push or the pull.

In Midnight Tides, he entered the game when he did not want the ascension of “the Pack” who escaped from the dying Azath Tower. The Pack was a d’ivers of six reptilian wolf-like beasts, as well as the god of the Jheck [soletaken Wolf people]. He failed to recruit Moroch Nevath and Bugg, but Iron Bars and the Crimson Guard were able to kill the Pack.
The Errant’s was attacked by B’nagga (a Jheck leader that followed Emperor Rhulad), but Iron Bars saved him. In return. The Errant escorted the Crimson Guard safely to their ships.
Back in the throne room, the Errant nudged Brys Beddict to drink from the poison cup that King Ezgara Diskanar drank from to kill himself before the Edur conquered the palace.
Tehol Beddict and Bugg are on a morning walk when a capabara fish crawls out out of the river and dies
A tentacled fish the size of a human but can grow big enough to try to mate with a galleon ship
Bugg carries it home for their dinner while Tehol continues to his appointment
Tehol sees guards acting like menacing police and remembers how their first mission was to raid and arrest the Rat Catcher's Guild
Scores of arrests were made, only to later be revealed the ones arrested were illusions
Tehol goes to Adventure Alley, where some shops have existed for 700 years
Enters the Half-Axe Temple of Herbs to trade a vial of capabara roe for a fat root
In the tiny cramped shop of Grool’s Immeasurable Pots, Tehol trades capabara spines for a beaker

In Beastmomger Shill’s small animals shop, to trade the fat root and beaker and is led down a trapdoor, through low ceiling snaking tunnels and beehive tombs, into the safe chamber where refugees and the fugitive Rat Catcher’s Guild master, Chief Investigator Rucket hides
Shill uses the fat root yellow tea to shrink the testicles of her animal, measured precisely with the beaker
Rucket praises Tehol for the spreading cracks in the foundation of an unspecified building
Rucket confirms Onyx completed the sixteen tablets with bevelled edges that Tehol requested
Tehol requests 50,000 for his plans which Rucket gladly grants if it’s against the Patriotists
Tehol wants to check to see if his balls shrank from handling the fat root, Rucket continues trying to sleep with him
Venitt Sathad and Rautos Hivanar discuss the Liberty’s Consign’s latest property purchase of an inn
A square building contains an iconic object that couldn't be removed and remains a storage closet
Shurq Elalle is now captain of her own pirate ship, the Undying Gratitude
Lost her first ship in a fiery encounter with a Mare escort (city in Lands of the Fist) in Laughter’s End, the ocean east of the Theft peninsula
Had sailed and delivered Iron Bars, Corlos, and the rest of their Crimson Guard group to the lands of Jacuruku, where they were last seen fighting large armored warriors
Iron Bars planned to cross the continent to the opposite coast, find a ship, and continue sailing
14 leagues west of the Draconean Isles, “First Mate” Skorgen Kaban spies a destroyed Edur Blackwood ship, Shurq Elalle decides they should search for loot
“Second mate” Misery sees that the blackwood ship is sinking
An amphora jar is found depicting hundreds crows surrounding a man crucified on an X-shaped cross
[Note: Coltaine?]
Skorgen recognizes the jars contained kagenza pollen that prevented blood from thickening, which Edur use to paint on their temples or trees
An Edur, who Skorgen recognized as Merude tribe, is found with hands and feet spiked to the floor and body methodically sliced up
Someome came to torture the Edur for information, only stole logs and charts
Shurq Elalle orders to burn the ship and set sail for Letheras

Shurq Elalle is a thief in Letheras that was cursed with undeath by one of her victims. Tehol and Bugg hired her to rob Gerun Eberict’s estate in exchange for giving her a makeover to feel alive, beautiful and an ootooloo parasite that allows her to have sex again. Shurq was the one that gave Kettle her name and gave her bodies to feed the dying Azath tower. During the heist, Shurq befriends Gerun’s dead brother, Harlest Eberict, and they ally to steal from the estate and escape together. After, Shurq is given a Jaghut tomb as a safehouse. Tehol also purchased a ship intending to be pirates with Shurq.

Shurq is hired for a second heist on the Tolls Repository, Kettle helps by recruiting thousands of ghosts that appear more alive as the Azath tower is dying. As the ghosts swarm the building, Shurq finds out who holds the largest royal debt. While on her way back, she falls onto a pile of trash and an iron spike impales her head. Tehol saws it off and covers it with a diamond-studded stopper.
Shurq sets sail as a pirate with Ublala Pung, Harlest Eberict, the Crimson Guard, and the women Tehol hired to help ferry people to refuge islands.
Redmask reflected on how the Letherii culture changed him
Banishment meant death for tribal people because they’re too stubborn to cooperate with others
The Letherii experienced spiritual punishment in different ways, and preferred Indebtedness to exile
Banishment sometimes was even beneficial, as an individual can be anonymous and start a new life in another city
The KCCM were off finding bhederin to eat. Sag’Churok would kill and let Gunth Mach eat first
Redmask enters the camp of the Renfayar clan, who only had six male warriors and women
No veterans, shouldermen, elders, or witches to guide them any longer
No picket lines, women screaming, and few rodara livestock

Masarch spoke first and was defensive until Redmask pointed out all of their mistakes, convincing them he is the real Redmask and not an impostor. Masarch says they've abandoned the old ways because it failed them
Masarch informs Redmask of the current situation
Aendinar clan wiped out. Sevond & Niritha clans join the Ganetok. The Ganetok are cowards, but are strong
The Ganetok made a pact with foreign mercenaries who worshiped the Wolves of War, and abandoned them to die against the Letherii about a year ago
A dray dog walked over and laid his head between Redmask’s feet
The foreign mercenaries didn't have wardogs, but did have dogs that followed them at a distance
Redmask becomes the leader of the Renfayar clan, decides to raid the Letherii to steal their livestock and to use them buy the services of the Ganetok warriors
Masarch curses the old traditions, Redmask slaps him unconscious and carries out a death night ritual, for Masarch to be buried in a coffin and climb out
Udinaas thinks about how Fear wants to kill him despite both of them abandoning Rhulad, Udinaas doing more than any of the Sengar family by being Rhulad’s friend
Thinks Seren Pedac has no reason to be here but still travels with them and holds onto Trull’s sword
The party walks across a mosaic floor that continues into the side chambers, depicting a war between K’Chain Che’Malle (long-tails) and K’Chain Nah'ruk (short tails)
Every scene showed the KC Nah'ruk as the victors, but defeated by a Matron’s sorcerous conflagrations
Silchas Ruin comments ‘Fouled K’ell, Naw’rhuk A’dat, and Matrons’
The party is near the surface, unknown of the exit will lead into a hostile fort
Seren is suspicious why this particular section is clean of bat droppings, doesn't want to trigger any traps evidenced by the fragments of archway structures blocking their path
Silchas explains the KC Nah’ruk carved vents and tubes that produces sound to repel bats, insects, and rodents. Not magic, wards, or curses
Udinaas bickers with Fear and says he lives to torment him, out of curiosity Silchas asks Udinaas what his motivation is
Udinaas mocks Silchas’s motivation as revenge
Near the end of the tunnel, Fear says Silchas might regret finding the fallen [Crippled] God
Kettle: ‘Why don't any of you like each other? I like all of you. Even Wither.’ Udinaas: 'It's alright, we're just tortured by who we are, Kettle.’ No one said much after that
Seren Pedac is scouting ahead, the cave opens to a forest at the top of the Bluerose Mountains
A garrison is nearby, scaled mice not afraid of humans runs across Seren’s boots, patrols are nearby
Seren returns to the cave and runs into Fear who was getting worried for her sake
Seren estimates 100-200 Letherii soldiers and mages
Silchas Ruin senses wards cast by the K’risnan that can't be avoided
Seren asks to put the garrison to sleep like Corlos of the Crimson Guard, but Silchas Ruin can't and doesn't know Mockra since it didn't exist during his time
Silchas recognizes the K’risnan sorcery, but riddled with chaos
Silchas marches forward to kill everyone in the garrison, regardless if they're soldiers or innocent staff or slaves, gather horses
Seren doesn't have the courage to stop him, tries to convince herself that she's only a guide, Udinaas sees right through her
Thousands of scaled mice flow towards Silchas Ruin
Ventrala, a K’risnan warlock, set up candles in a ritual to Sister Shadow
[Note: Sheltatha Lore, daughter of Scabandari Bloodeye aka Father Shadow]
Ventrala sensed orthen, the scaled mice, were swarming towards the garrison
Ventrala’s body surged with power that didn't belong to Sheltatha Lore
Ventrala senses [Silchas Ruin’s] bloodlust coming
Atri-Preda Hayenar, military commander of a city, was commanded to pursue Udinaas’s group
K’risnan Ventrala escorted by x25 Merude tribe Edur joined the mission to her disgust
Alarm bells and shouting wake her up
K’risnan Ventrala probed his senses toward [Silchas Ruin], followed by Silchas’s ‘vast cold power’ slamming him against the wall and pushing Ventrala’s own power into himself
A fort wall explodes
Atri-Preda Hayenar runs into the street and sees the bastion into the city had been breached, black fire burns the building rubble, orthen scaled mice swarm and eat corpses and horses
Silchas Ruin approaches with his dual blades, parries all spears thrown by the Merude, then proceeds to decapitate, disembowel, and sever limbs as they charged
Hayenar is afraid of how gleeful the sound of the blades are
Hayenar shouts for her soldiers to retreat, a Merude demands her to stay and fight or he would kill her instead
Ventrala curls up in the corner of the room
The mission to capture Udinaas and Fear was commanded by Hannan Mosag alone, who planned to use them to destroy Rhulad and take back his throne
The Crippled God’s power feeds on the flaws and imperfections of the soul which manifests in destroying the vessel’s flesh and bones, thus granting the vessel power
Because the Crippled God doesn't want to face Silchas Ruin, his power had fled from Ventrala
Ventrala feels betrayed having his flesh sacrificed and being sent on this futile mission
Ventrala realizes ‘Pain was not to be embraced. Chaos is anathema to a mortal body. It ruined flesh because it did not belong there. There is no exultation in self-destruction’
A wraith [Wither] enters the room, mocks Ventrala, proclaims Silchas Ruin a ‘pale king of the orthen’
Wither’s chains to the Edur were severed by Silchas, whom he now serves
The Atri-Preda was smart enough to flee with her Letherii soldiers, all of the Merude are dead
Silchas Ruin enters with a swarm of orthen and asks who is his enemy
Ventrala says the Crippled God had fled and was not involved, it was Hannan Mosag’s deed alone
Silchas reveals that the visions the Azath gave him during his internment showed him events all around the world
Silchas spares Ventrala’s life so he could deliver a message to Hannan Mosag
A god in pain is not the same as a god obsessed with evil. Hannan Mosag’s obsessions are his own and he seems he is the one confused
Warns not to fuck with him again
Silchas leaves to find some horses which was the reason to come to the fort, the orthen scaled mice also withdraw
Ventrala agrees to find Atri-Preda Hayenar to escort him to deliver Silchas’ message to Hannan Mosag
Believes Silchas knows the most about the Crippled God and feels pity, not hate for him
‘You should close a better god to worship, Ventrala. Tortured spirits
like company, even a god's. Then again, perhaps it is the likes of
who have in turn shape the Crippled God. Perhaps, without his
broken, malformed worshippers, he would have healed long ago’
Night time, almost dawn. Seren and the party hear the destruction of the fort, Kettle laughs in a ‘disgusting way’. Silchas returns with horses
Silchas decides it's time he and Fear discuss their objective of searching for Scabandari Bloodeye’s soul
Fear wants to find Scabandari so that he could help free Rhulad and the Tiste Edur from the Crippled God
Fear accepts the truth that Scabandari betrayed Silchas, but does not know how the Tiste Edur can make reparations to Silchas
Silchas knew that Scabandari had betrayed Andarist and his plans, Silchas planned to betray Scabandari as well but did not expect Scabandari to be so blatant
Silchas does not want Scabandari’s soul to be freed, thinks it's not enough to free the Tiste Edur from the Crippled God

Silchas thinks Hannan Mosag is aware of Silchas, that Scabandari’s soul may already be used by someone, and that the Tiste Edur will be free when he makes his move against the Crippled God. After that, they can speak of reparations
Seren tells them that they should ride until midday, asks for assurance that they won't be chased, and if there were wards at all
Silchas's silence implies he may have lied about the wards
As Seren prepares the new horses, Udinaas watches Kettle play with a friendly orthen scaled mouse
Wither appears and reveals the orthen are from the K’Chain Che'Malle world, larger ones bred for food, some escaped into the mountains
Wither is disappointed that Udinaas feels familiar enough to interrupt and disrespect Wither, with how much he knows
Udinaas surprises Wither when he says he grieves for Kettle’s innocence when they inevitably kill her

Redmask travels with two new-blooded young warriors (Theven, and Kraysos) and the young Awl leader Masarch towards a Letherii drover camp led by the Factor’s foreman as he ponders the history of the Awl people and the KCCM
There were 17 Awl legends describing the battles against the Kechra, aka K’Chain Che'Malle which are considered the Firstborn of dragons
Although the Awl become proficient in battling the KCCM, they were only one of many obstacles against the KCCM’s desperate fleeing
The KCCM came from the west lands, presently the Letherii Empire, and traveled east past Awl lands
In Redmask’s life experience, he's learned that his world of the Awl was just one of many ropes that knot and intertwine against the eternity of struggle
The Awl fought against the Letherii’s greed in owning other lands
At the settlement was herds of thousands of rodara (a herd animal with horns, long necks, blue back), Redmask and the three young warriors get ready to attack
(Abasard)
Abasard, a 16 year old boy, used to live with his big family in the filthy slums of Drene until they joined the Factor’s foreman to the Awl lands
Leaving the city, the plains was an extraordinary place to them. Several family members had been healed of their illnesses and started smiling and laughing for the first time
Abasard follows his fogs to see what disturbs the rodara herd
Abasard finds one dog with its throat sliced open and the other dog with its neck broken, both happening simultaneously
The rodara herd appeared to be alert to ‘someone they're used to obeying’
Abasard returns back to the drover camp
(Redmask)
Redmask beheads a shepherd, cuts of his face, and places it in a bag full of salt
Enjoys delivering Awl vengeance
Heads towards the screams coming from drover camp
(Abasard)
Abasard returns to camp and sees the youth Masarch kill a man and his family
Abasard tries to save his little sister, but is cut in half
Doesn't regret learning and seeing the outside world
Young Awl leader Masarch watched as the rodara herd followed Redmask
Watches as the KCCM slaughtered a Letherii camp in the distance
Now trusts that Redmask will be the one to defeat the Ganetok warleader and lead the war against the Letherii
Considers Redmask his war leader
(Azath Tower, Hannan Mosag)
Hannan Mosag approached ruins of a dead Azath Tower, senses remnants of a Kurald Galain binding ritual, and an entity beginning to free itself
Vinik, turtles with clawed paws and thumbs, were in their mating season
(Alleyway, Sukul Ankhadu)
A woman with diluted Tiste Edur blood leads a potential rapist into an alleyway and eats him
[Note: Will be revealed as Sukul Ankhadu in the last scene of this chapter, personally I find it unnecessary to hide her identity to the reader]
Senses someone (Hannan Mosag) interfering with Silchas Ruin’s binding wards. Suspects the Errant or Mael
Hannan Mosag was the Warlock King of the Tiste Edur. He united the six Tiste Edur tribes, and held the sons of each tribe chieftain hostage as his personal warlock cadre, the K’risnan.

Hannan Mosag’s power came from a bargain with the Crippled God, which let him control a ‘demon spirit-god’ that helped him unite the tribes and conquer the Letherii empire. The ‘demon spirit-god’ was actually one of six Forgotten Gods that Mael helped fashion dolmens to preserve their existence and guarded by a ‘Guardian of Names’. Brys Beddict visited this sanctuary and saw one of the six dolmens was empty.

Hannan Mosag sent the Sengar brothers to retrieve a sword, forged by the Meckros smith Withal and gifted by the Crippled God. However, Hannan Mosag was planning to betray the Crippled God all along, to use the power to protect the Tiste Edur rather than to conquer. Knowing this, the Crippled God let the cursed sword fall into Rhulad’s hands manipulating him to be Emperor. Hannan Mosag became his servant.

Hannan Mosag and the K’risnan led the Tiste Edur to conquer the Letherii Empire. In the throne room, he used the bodies of the captive Queen Janall and Prince Quillas to fuel his sorcerous battle with Ceda Kuru Qan. The cost of using the Crippled God’s power left Hannan Mosag disfigured and crippled.
These three people have the most convoluted and contradictory lineage ever, probably intentionally unclear on Erikson’s part. They are definitely Tiste, but hard to tell if they’re Liosan or Edur.

Osserc (Liosan, son of Father Light) was the father of Sukul Ankhadu (who looks more Edur) and Menandore (who looks more Liosan). Their ritual mother was T’iam, so the daughters are eleint. That makes them technically half-brothers with L’oric. Being a ritual mother was metaphorical for the daughters to be eleint. Scabandari Bloodeye (Father Shadow) was the father of Sheltatha Lore. Her ritual mother was also T’iam, so she’s an eleint. Sukul Ankhadu and Menandore consider Sheltatha Lore their cousin, because T’iam being the ritual mother doesn’t really matter. I’m not sure why she’s a ‘cousin’, but distant relations.

After Udinaas was possessed by Wyval blood, he encountered Menandore in a dream. Menandore took interest in his situation and raped him and later gives birth to Rud Ellale. Menandore dropped him off in a Meckros city to be raised by Meckros parents. When the Crippled God destroyed the Meckros city (not the same city Withal lived in), Menandore rescued Rud Elalle and the surviving Meckros and placed them in a realm [later identified as the Refugium] where mortal Bentract Imass lived. The Imass promised to take care of Rud Ellale until Menandore returned.
Ulshun Pral, a Bentract Imass, told Udinaas and Feather Witch that the sisters Sukul Ankhadu and Menandore had closed off the Hold of Dragons, Starvald Demelain, long ago.
In another dream, Udinaas saw Sukul Ankhadu and Menandore drag their ‘cousin’, Sheltatha Lore, and buried her in the Azath Tower. Sheltatha Lore is still buried there as far as we know.
Rautos Hivanar watches as work crews continue to excavate the river below searching for mysteries artifacts that fit into a mechanism
He grants Venitt Sathad extra men and supplies to investigate Factor Lectur Anict in Drene for “losing perspective”. Letur Anict’s work for the Liberty Consign was unsatisfactory
[Note: Because he was very focused on waging war against the Awl for personal gain]
Orbyn Truthfinder (Patriotist) will be their ally
Vinik nests were floating down the river, a large vinik turtle eats one of the nest unseen
Tehol Beddict ponds over his brown eye and blue eye
Bugg unloads his godly burdens and gives an info dump, unsure what to do
The Errant follows Hannan Mosag to see what he's up to
Hannan Mosag is messing with a ritual, another ascendant (Sukul Ankhadu) is going to meet him and they partner up to free something chained (below the Azath tower)
Freeing that thing will disturb something up north (???) but they can't do anything yet
The Edur fleet returns to Letheras with two champions [Icarium and Karsa Orlong] who may not be able to kill Rhulad
Scabandari Bloodeye’s soul will be revealed
Karos Invictad is pursuing Tehol for bankrupting the empire
Bugg may have put a mosquito net on Tehol to sorcerously hide him. Maybe.
Bugg prepares poisonous vinik eggs, improvising the herbs that would make them less poisonous
Tehol makes a quip that Bugg should improvise to solve his godly burdens in similar way
Tanal Yathvanar received a puzzle box from an urchin to deliver to Karos Invictad
An opened top box. Inside is a two-headed insect perpetually rotating in place and will starve to death in four months. It won't eat while rotating but can drink water from moss
The challenge is to rearrange the polished tiles inside the box that will stop the insect from rotating
Janath Anar tries to keep herself mentally occupied by reciting an early history lecture, aka an info dump
Keden Qan, the Royal Engineer for the first 50-60 years of the Letherii Empire had discovered that the city was built upon the ruins of a Jaghut civilization pre-diaspora and upon the Azath Tower
Presently, three Jaghut towers remained behind the Old Palace
However, the Jaghut tower and Azath tower were not the first to occupy these lands, they built their civilization on top of a pre-existing one

A fortress city where even the alley ways, streets, and plazas were roofed with multiple layers. And still a second more defensible could be found deeper within, and is presently used for Letheras’ sewage system
No potsherds, sculptures, metal workings, or any other artifacts remained
Evidence of desperate failed attempts to install insulation suggested the civilization ended because of catastrophic climate change
Tanal Yathvanar appears to keep Janath Anar alive with some water
Janath is chained up, stomach acids eating through her skin, wishing the candle was extinguished so she couldn't see the maggots crawling in her feces
Tanal and Janath taunt each other, Janath speaks on a 2nd century cult that believed every victim in a person’s life would await and meet that person in the after life
The head priest was torn limb from limb in the streets, but the cult lives on with the people victimized by the Letheras Empire - the Tarthenal, Fent, and Nerek
Tanal responds that Karos Invictad had written a treatise that those who failed create justifications for themselves
Janath lashes back that Karos was a failure of a student. Some incident, possibly a betrayal by a lover or colleague, had turned Karos into a victim.
Thus the man lashes out against the world, which will never end because he will always see himself as a victim
Tanal slaps her twice, knocking her unconscious
POV change, Tanal leaves the prison in haste and anxiety
Tanal believes Karos will purge the Letheras Empire of all non-Letherii humans and return to the glory of the First Empire
Convinces himself that victims like Janath Anar learn to enjoy pain
Still, Janath had shaken Tanal’s believes and now her voice in his head makes him second guess himself

cards.h: Scene 7 (Eternal Domicile & Refuge warren, the Errant)

i.html: The Errant returns after stalking Hannan Mosag at the Azath Tower; walks in the empty Eternal Domicile palace pondering how on gods persist on meagre existence before being forgotten
The Jaghut understood futility, considers Gothos’ Folly a multi-volumed suicide note [Note: lmao]
The Errant decides to visit Menandore and walks effortlessly into a warren with a flower field and vermillion sky. A place Menandore considers her refuge
Cryptic conversation
Sky keeps somehow involved (KCCM)
Menandore’s sisters have plans that will incidentally have Menandore killed
A female entity will be imminently free
[Note: Probably Sheltatha Lore under the Azath Tower]
There are others (ascendants?) plotting in Letheras
The Errant is annoyed and returns to the Eternal Domicile
Menandore watches as Shadowthrone and Hood approaches
Shadowthrone offers to help Menandore against her sisters in exchange for access to Starvald Demelain. A convergence of desires is coming
[Note: Menandore and Sukul Ankhadu had closed the Hold of Starvald Demelain, they’re daughters of T’iam]
Nisall visits the former queen Janall who is surprisingly still alive in a very malformed and twisted body
Janall claims to be the Queen [of High House Chains]
The position of King in Chains is indifferent to the occupant
Nisall warns that Chancellor Triban Gnol is the reason for Rhulad’s failures and Karos Invictad is attempting to usurp the Edur
Janall claims her Master [the Crippled God] sees through her eyes, that he is almost done with using the Edur and is dissatisfied with Rhulad
Nisall leaves promising her loyal servants will take care of her and give her a canopy bed
Janall and the Crippled God have a conversation using her voice, like Gollum and Smeagol
Janall demands her throne as Queen of Chains
The Crippled God says he is in as much agony and is as insane as his followers wanted him to be. They made him this way
The Crippled God agrees to give her the throne, but warns her “we all die”
[Note: This is the last time Janall is ever mentioned in the series]
Nisall leaves, reflecting on Janall’s ambitions just as strong as ever and sensed the Crippled God’s presence in her
Thinks about the war conspiracy against the Bolkando border alliance

Nisall runs into Bruthen Trana who agrees that Chancellor Triban Gnol and Invigilator Karos Invictad are tightly controlling the information that is communicated to Rhulad, encouraging the wars against the border nations
Bruthen reveals that Karos Invictad has a plot to arrest Nisall for sedition
The two agree to team up, Bruthen assigns two Edur bodyguards for Nisall
Nisall urges the need for subtlety
He responds, ‘Nisall, we are children of Shadow’
Sukul Ankhadu arrives at the Azath Tower and sees creatures who escaped death. Those creatures remind her of when she walked through Hood’s realm
Hood’s realm was also known as Festal’rythan, eleint word meaning ‘Layers of the Dead’ in which all life and species could be found trapped in layers of sediment
Sukul Ankhadu approaches Hannan Mosag
Hannan Mosag thought he would find Sheltatha Lore here, as well as hoping to find Scabandari Bloodeye’s Finnest
Views Sukul Ankhadu as the cruelest sister
Sukul Ankhadu reveals she wants to release Sheltatha Lore because she worked better with her than Menandore
Hannan Mosag wants to obtain Scabandari’s Finnest so the Crippled God can use its power in the war that will come to the gods
Wants to ally with Sukul Ankhadu to defeat Silchas Ruin in exchange for somehow stopping her need to eat people and also destroying the Finnest after
Hannan Mosag leaves before Sheltatha Lore is freed, or else she would've eaten him

Shurq Elalle and the Undying Gratitude crew are sailing from the Draconean Sea to Letheras and want to beat the Letheras/Edur fleet so they can make the most profit off their loot (which was taken from an Edur ship)
[Note: The same fleet bringing Icarium and Karsa Orlong]
First mate Skorgen Kaban is worried they found the sunken ship and are chasing them, convinces Shurq Elalle to sell their loot on a prison isle near Fent Reach controlled by its former prisoners
Skorgen prays to several sea spirits
The Face Under the Waves, the Guardian of the Drowned, the Swallower of Ships, the Stealer of Winds, the Tower of Water, the Reef Hiders
Fent prophecy that one day their names will rise from the waters and the world will be underwater, evidenced by Fent maps showing their founding cities are now sunken underwater
The Edur also have claims that ice far too the north are breaking apart and ocean levels will rise over the next several thousand years
All an allegory for rising sea levels and climate change
Shurq Elalle calls for their youngest member, Burdenar, to sleep with her in her cabin
Before leaving Letheras, Venitt Sathad visits an inn that Rautos Hivanar purchased and contracted Bugg’s Construction to refurbish
During the remodeling, a large metal edifice was uncovered. Bent at a 90 degree angle with no seams, one of Rautos Hivanar’s artifacts was an exact replica
Venitt Sathad discusses with Bugg, Bugg had seen several similar structures buried in silt around Letheras
Venitt wishes for Bugg to deliver a message in person to Rautos Hivanar that he should see the metal structure in person and to bring his artifacts
Bugg asks about the shoring-up project at Hivanar’s estate, Venitt reveals the purpose is to uncover more artifacts buried underneath
They bid each other farewell
Atri-Preda Bivatt and Brohl Handar walk through the aftermath of the KCCM’s slaughter of the Letherii drover camps
Brohl grieves for the children killed on both sides, that both sides are losers. The only winners are people like Letur Anict who profit off the dead
Brohl, being a slave owner himself, compares the Letherii soldiers to slaves
Bivatt is offended and shaken, leaves the dead Letherii as the continue to move on
Doesn't want to curse them by burying them with stones covered in Awl glyphs
Redmask leads the young Awl Renfayar clan warriors and the herd of rodara to the Ganetok encampment, which also includes the remnant Sevond and Niritha clans
Redmask and co. are surrounded by the Ganetok, the leader Hadralt speaks out with a dozen warriors that painted their faces in copper scales, copper masks
Redmask summons the KCCM, and calls the Ganetok cowards for abandoning their allies
A coppermask breaks down and reveals Hadralt had poisoned his father so the Ganetok clan would not war against the Letherii
Hadralt claimed that the Awl would not survive against the Letherii and instead traded with them to receive iron weapons
Redmask reveals Hadralt was bribed by the Letherii with money, property in Drene, and indebted slaves to betray his own people by giving them inferior weapons
The coppermasks stab Hadralt in the back, killing him
Redmask claims leadership of the Ganetok

‘Seeds fall from the crown of the stalk. What is flawed there makes its every child weak. The curse of cowardice has ended this day. We are the Awl, and I am your war leader. And so I shall lead you to war’
Masarch, Kraysos, and Theven speak about their faith in Redmask’s success
Kraysos and Theven tried to cheat the death night burial, but their “bledden herbs” wore off quick and they went through the full experience
All of them now follow Redmask in earnest
Brohl Handar, Atri-Preda Bivatt, and her Letherii army are half a day away from Drene
Brohl thinks about how important the Bluerose Mountains region are as a supply route, any problems would doom Drene if the Awl started a war
Bluerose was annexed into the Letherii Empire, but rebel groups as well as a mysterious priesthood that united Bluerose opponents of the Empire still existed
[Note: The Onyx Order of Bluerose Tiste Andii that worship Anomander Rake, will come up later]
Brohl wonders how the Overseer is Bluerose is managing
Bivatt explains that the Letherii have surplus harvests of grain to trade for Bluerose’s supplies of minerals, metals, lumber, and fish. Markets from the far south import slaves and luxury foodstuffs
She believes the Letherii will have no shortages of material resources

Brohl reveals to Bivatt of Letur Anict’s illegal smuggling of low quality weapons and armor sold to the Awl [confirms that Hadralt did intend to betray the Ganetok, Redmask was speaking truth] in exchange for land
Brohl also reveals that a fortress in the Bluerose Mountains had been destroyed
[Note: Probably referring to Silchas Ruin’s attack to get some horses]
Brohl asks if the Letherii have enough forces for victory
Bivatt believes the Awl has 8,000-9,000 warriors between several rival feuding clans, experienced with raids and ambushes
The Letherii has x6 companies of the Bluerose Battalion, Artisan Battalion, Drene Garrison, x4 companies of the Harradict Brigade, the Crimson Rampart Brigade, and half of the Merchants’ Battalion
[Note: None of these individual groups are important to remember]
Brohl wants Redmask dead ASAP
Bivatt wants the Awl to be enslaved and scattered away from their homelands
Same fate of the Nerek, Fent, and Tarthenal
Brohl curses Redmask for giving hope to the Awl and giving Letur Anict all the reasons he needs to exterminate the Awl
Redmask calls a meeting with the clan leaders and elders to plan a new way to fight the Letherii, but doesn't go there right away
The ambushes and raids of the Awl will fail
Not enough time or experience to teach the Letherii way of fighting
Redmask thinks about how the Ganetok sold land to hire a foreign army to fight against the Letherii
Hadralt got greedy, left the army to die and keep the money
The army is the Grey Swords wielding a Lamatath [Note: Genabaris region] banner, they came to fulfill a prophecy to fight in the Battlefield of the Gods
Toc the Younger/Unlucky in Anaster’s body is being held behind the Awl women’s bleeding hut, half buried and soaked in blood
Toc says his visions expected him to meet the First Sword of the KCCM, did not expect it to be a human and jokes that he hopes the mask was enough to fool them
K’ell Champion. Consort to the Matron. King.
Clip, a is a 19 year old Bluerose Tiste Andii mixed with Nerek, Letherii, and D’rasilhani
Tall, thin, long midnight black hair, face smooth with no wrinkles, eyes of firerock
Wears a black hide shirt, a bow, teardrop-shaped X pattern arrows
A baldric slung rapier in a turtle shell scabbard lined with sheepskin
Has a habit of fidgeting with a chain and a ring on each side, spins it and wraps it around his finger
Clip is from the hidden village of Andara, where the order of the Onyx Wizards worship Anomander Rake and have strict rules, traditions, and responsibilities that the younger members hate
Clip cast away his named and exiled himself, but still feels compelled to obey the orders of Ordant Brid, Reve Master of the Rock
Clips walks on and approaches Seren Pedac’s group, is stopped by Wither
Clip recognizes Wither as a Tiste Andii spirit that was a slave to the Tiste Edur. Also recognizes Silchas Ruin as his god’s brother
Wither thinks he'll fit right in with the group
Seren Pedac and Silchas Ruin speak with Clip, as Udinaas holds Kettle asleep in his arms
Clip had been tasked by Ordant Brid to bring Silchas to Andara via Kurald Galain
Silchas Ruin would not find [Scabandari Bloodeye’s soul] in either Bluerose, Jasp, or Outbound
The Onyx Order has knowledge that Rake expected Silchas Ruin to be free eventually.
Because [Gothos] scattered the Tiste Edur with Omtose Phellack powerful enough to stop death on the continent, Rake ignored the Edur, too busy with other matters
Kurald Emurlahn being sundered, Osserc being nearby, Lady Envy, a shaky alliance with Kilmandaros, and Silanah who emerged from Emurlahn
Clip annoys Silchas enough to almost be decapitated, but dodges out of the way
Clip opens a portal to Kurald Galain which they all begrudgingly enter
Seren Pedac asks why he does that [fidget with the chain], Clip annoyingly but honestly asks “do what”
Book Two:
Layers of the Dead
The Tiste Edur fleet has returned home to Letheras after sailing the world in search for champions that can kill Rhulad
Atri-Preda Yan Tovis (aka Twilight), Taralack Veed, Icarium, Tomad Sengar, Uruth Sengar, Hanradi Khalag
Scores of ships lost,  thousands of Letherii marines dead
Taralack Veed comes up to watch the approach of the city with Yan Tovis
Taralack assures Icarium will fight, has embraced his curse, and feels excited
Yan Tovis noticed several banners flying over the Eternal Domicile, none were Tiste Edur
Believes Chancellor Triban Gnol had schemed the poison that killed King Ezgara Diskanar [Note: and Brys Beddict], and has slowly usurped power from the Tiste Edur
Taralack Veed says Rhulad will die eventually even without Icarium

‘I do not speak of Icarium now. I speak of when a god’s chosen one fails. And they always do, Twilight. We are never enough in their eyes. Never faithful enough, never fearful enough, never abject enough. Sooner or later we betray them, in weakness or in overwrought ambition. We see before ud a city of bridges yet what I see and what you see are two different things. Do not let your eyes deceive you - the bridges awaiting us are all too narrow for mortals’
The Errant watches from a distance as the Letherii Fleet disembarks
Tomad Sengar, Taralack Veed, Icarium
Atri-Preda Yan Tovis, whom the Errant feels has a fate about her
Frustrated that his powers are weaker, not knowing what her fate is
Hadn't felt this weak since the T’lan Imass toppled the First Empire of Dessimbelackis
The Errant recognizes Icarium as Gothos’ son and a true challenge to Rhulad
Feels the ritual of the Nameless Ones on Icarium
The stain of Azath blood feels like a cloud around Icarium
Icarium’s mother was an “overgrown hag”
[Note: From a 2020 fan question, Erikson says it's impossible to know who his mother is from the published text thus far]
As Icarium steps onto Letheras, an earthquake occurs, a building [Note: Scale House] collapses in the distance, and a smoke cloud rises
Icarium smiles
Taralack Veed tells Yan Tovis that Burn, the sleeping goddess, twitched (earthquake) because of Icarium
Yan Tovis dismisses it, but affirms that earthquakes occur to the mountain ranges to the far north and far south. But does not occur in Lether itself
Yan Tovis says Taralack Veed and Icarium will be given their quarters, Rhulad will challenge him whenever he feels like it whether it be immediately or weeks later
A burial urn will be immediately prepared for all challengers
Taralack Veed returns to Icarium’s side to encourage him
Icarium feels that he's been here before the city was born, perhaps the reason why he did not refuse Taralack Veed which surprises Taralack
Jaghut had been on Icarium’s trail
Omtose Phellack ice is the heart of the city Lether [Note: Gothos freezing the continent]
Icarium is excited that he will discover his secrets at last
Taralack Veed is now afraid to die
Karsa Orlong snaps some rats’ necks, bored as he bickers with Samar Dev
The Edur have the bodies of the enslaved Edur from Sepik, jars of spiced human blood, and Sepik’s conch shell throne
Karsa hears thousands of Samar Dev’s spirits crying out in his head
When Karsa lit the candles in Samar Dev’s home, he released spirits trapped in the wax. Samar Dev trapped those spirits in her knife
Samar Dev is aware there are resident gods in Lether
Samar can sense Bairoth Gild and Delum Thord within Karsa’s sword
Karsa and Samar head above the deck, Karsa demands for Havok and to get off the ship
The captain knows by now it's hopeless to talk back
Karsa arrives onto Lether, on the gangplank the Letherii guards demand Karsa be unarmed and to come with them to the compound
Karsa grabbed and tossed the guard into the air, into three other port workers like bowling pins
Karsa punches a second guard, who reached for his sword, in the face and knocks him out
A half circle of guards gather around, Karsa demands if they're his escort then they better be civil and again demands for Havok
Bugg stands nearby from the Hivanar estate entrance. Feels nervous that Icarium has arrived
‘Death is written in birth’, words of a sage whose name Bugg has forgotten
Remembers witnessing Icarium come from the sea after destroying a realm. Had come to see his father, but Gothos went into an Azath
[Note: Icarium had attempted to free his father from a Azath house in the Jhag odhan which broke Icarium’s mind. Gothos currently resides in the Deadhouse of Malaz City]
A nearby servant interrupts Bugg’s thoughts, talks about Scale House had fallen after flooding, the only fatality was a cat
[Note: The Rat Catcher’s Guild, an assassination group disguised as a rat catching and odd jobs organization]
Investigated the disappearance of thousands of Letherii citizens in the past year
[Note: Tehol hired the guild to escort refugees to a private island]
On Hivanar’s terrace, Bugg watches his employees work the pumps that emptied the riverbank around the estate
Hivanar has uncovered several artifacts he has been unable to assemble, also stone chips and shards found in layers below where the artifacts were found
Bugg recites a memory, an Eres’al couple that were here for three seasons. The woman died in childbirth, the man carried the baby but the baby also died
The man could find no other fellow Eres’al after their people were scattered when fires took over the great forest and plains
Mentions Icarium said there would be no end, ‘that the cut thread was but an illusion’
Bugg does that elaborate further, says a piece with the seamless right angle has an identical larger piece in Hivanar’s recently refurbished inn
The pieces don’t fit into each other, a central piece is missing and they're connected by energy ‘that has yet to arrive’
[Note: Assuming these are Icarium’s mechanical inventions, Icarium is what powers them]
Bugg walks out to the terrace, Hivanar follows him like a puppy unsure what to ask or say
Bugg walks off into the street, leaving Hivanar behind. Two of Karos Invictad’s Patriotists walks by, one is upset because he probably was almost bumped into. Unclear, but he a bitch
Bugg straight up calls them out for their criminal acts as police, they threaten him with a Drowning
Irony as Bugg is Mael, Elder God of the Sea
Bugg loses his temper and transports them to make them meet something ‘bigger and meaner’, embarrassed that he performed his sorcery in a very public setting
Feather Witch creeps around the crypts underneath the Old Palace while thinking about the people brought to Lether
Tiste Edur mix-bloods from Sepik, seen more disgraceful than slaves, Nemil fisher folk, x4 copper skinned Shal Morzinn warriors taken from a sinking ship
Seven Cities natives from Ehrlitan, Karang Isles, Pur Atrii, etc
Malazan sailors from Quon
Genabackan natives from Lamatath and Callows
The notable challengers are
An axeman from a ruined Meckros City that the Edur fleet raided, Cabalhii monk, A silent woman wearing a porcelain mask with 11 arcane glyphs on its brow, found near Callows
[Note: I'm guessing this is a Seguleh]
Feather Witch is astonished how many different languages and cultures dedicated themselves to so many gods that don't care about them, only use them as fodder for their ‘self-destructive wars’
Feather Witch vows to supercede the gods, to use these crypts as a path to obtain the “throne of oblivion”
[Note: This is not an actual throne in the series, more like a cheeky comment]
In the storage rooms of the Old Palace crypts, Feather Witch had plenty food, water, clothing, and reading material from the Imperial Library
Histories of the peoples subjugated by the Letherii Empire over the past 7-8 centuries
Nerek, Fent, Tarthenal, Bratha, Katter, Dresh, Shake
Written in arcane Letherii and a language FW doesn’t recognize
Thinks about the First Empire, how it claims to be the first human empire
Feather Witch sits down and brings out her ‘favorite possession’ she keeps in a leather pouch as Hannan Mosag appears
Hannan Mosag recognizes FW has enough power as a Ceda and wants to work with her to destroy Rhulad, take back the Tiste Edur, and return home to the north
FW remembers how cruelly the Edur treated the Letherii slaves, though indebtedness is worse because it spreads to every family member and generation
