Hannan Mosag regrets touching the Crippled God’s power, had intended to use the god to unite the Edur tribes and avoid any wars to live in peaceful isolation
Hannan Mosag planned to use Rhulad’s family to destroy him, but FW reveals that several are dead
Uruth and Tomad are afraid of Rhulad
Binadas is confirmed dead by Tomad’s dream and Hanradi Khalag failing to find his soul
Trull chained in the Nascent
Fear had run away
Hannan Mosag doubles down, that the Letherii are enough to sabotage themselves and hints at a war to the east
Feather Witch joins him
Rhulad sits on his throne with Nisall at his side and Chancellor Triban Gnol as his audience
Triban Gnol reports of Binadas’ death, and that his killer [Karsa Orlong] has arrived as a challenger
They believe Karsa carried the souls of the thousands he's slaughtered including Binadas
Rhulad believes everyone is plotting against him, that his father wants the challenger to kill Rhulad because Rhulad killed his own brothers
Triban Gnol also reports that Invigilator Karos Invictad believes there's a traitor among the Edur
Rhulad’s fear of his fellow Edur becomes validated in his mind because an outside agent is affirming it
Triban Gnol is dismissed
Nisall attempt to calm Rhulad, to speak against Karos and state that both Tomad and Bruthen Trana have been trying to speak to Rhulad daily, but have been turned away by Triban Gnol every single time
Rhulad does not know who to believe and tells her to get washed and in bed
Bruthen Trana approaches Tomad to say all Edur have been kept away from Rhulad, and that Hannan Mosag is not to be trusted
Bruthen Trana believes Nisall is their key to success, but Tomad dismisses her as Triban Gnol’s puppet and walks away
Karos Invictad is still unable to solve the insect puzzle
Tanal Yathvanar says the puzzle must be rigged because Karos hasn’t solved it yet
Karos insults Tanal for being so pathetic and stupid and unable to push beyond his capacity
Tanal Yathvanar reports Triban Gnol’s success in have Rhulad be suspicious of his fellow Edur
Karos wants Tanal to arrest Nisall, as a reward she can be Tanal’s next victim
Karos also thinks its too late to free Janath Anar and best just have her dead now
Tanal Yathvanar believes he's in love with Janath Anar and wants to run away with her
Tanal believes he is superior to Karos Invictad and will defy him so
Arriving at the torture chamber, Janath Anar regrets not being able to void her bowels all over him
Tanal unshackles her and she falls unconscious
Tanal carries her to the last of many domed chambers containing wells used to toss bodies and feed white shell crabs
Tanal shackles her between two corpses, deludedly believes eventually she’ll learn to love him and he leaves

cards.h: Scene 13, 14 (Corpse disposal well, Janath Anar, Bugg)

i.html: Janath listens as Tanal walks away. She admits defeat, believing his insanity can only be met with madness in kind but failed
A man with a weathered face unshackles her and picks her up
Bugg picks Janath Anar up in his arms, contemplating the ancient structures they are in
The Quillas River flower over a layer a silt that was a story thick (about 14 ft or 4 meters)
Underneath the silt layer was ruins of an ancient city, flooded when the river dramatically changed coarse millenia ago
The tunnels and wells somehow remained dry, its walls a sponge to drain water. Its ancient wells were used by the Patriotists to bury 16,000 Letherii
Bugg wanted to unleash his full fury on the Patriotists, but knows it would attract unwanted attention that would lead to indiscriminate slaughter
Tehol Beddict had decided that Karos Invictad must go, Bugg is eager to carry it out
Tehol Beddict is making awful soup, complains to Ublala Pung that Bugg is getting too big of a head and needs a whack
Ublala isn’t with Shurq Elalle because he was too big to sleep below decks and it wasn't fun
Ublala reports that a challenger has arrived, a Tarthenal [Note: Karsa] as pure blood as the Seregahl. One worthy of true worship
Ublala will group up with [Karsa] and wait to see if they should follow him
Ublala can smell the spirits that follow Karsa

Tehol shares that Rucket sent a person to report that Scale House had collapsed from an unnatural earthquake, and that the Rat Catcher’s Guild believes there is a challenger more frightening than what Ublala reports
Bugg arrives carrying Janath Anar, Tehol says there’s no room in the cauldron for her body
Tehol recognizes Janath as a lecturer that a lot of the boys had crushes on
Ublala whacks Bugg on the head, Bugg blames Tehol for forgetting to speak plainly to Ublala
Bugg thinks the Patriotists will conduct a manhunt for someone already deemed “vanished”
Ublala laughs thinking the Patriotists are stupid to be hunting a man and not a woman
A longhouse with a stable and coop outbuildings was taken from another realm to be a farm for the people and children that survived defending the First Throne. Panek, Aystar, Trull, Onrack, Quick Ben
Quick Ben wants to go home, but can't simply travel via warren because the Shadow warren is constantly moving, may end up in an ocean
Cotillion admits the Azath have fixed gates he could use
Quick Ben found out the Shadow warren has usurped the original gate of Kurald Emurlahn
Cotillion says it was necessary because the warren needing healing after being shattered
Quick Ben wonders if the Azath is intelligent, or a force that acts like a biological immune system. Wonders whose blood are the Elder warrens from, if K’rul’s blood is used for the warrens
Cotillion says he has ‘a key’ for Quick Ben, Trull, and Onrack
Cotillion affirms that Shadowthrone saved Kalam’s life, Kalam is inside the Deadhouse healing until his poison wears off. Does not say why, ‘be glad I didn't tell you the real reason’
Trull Sengar has a new stone spear and is wearing a burgundy cape
Onrack senses the other side of the lake does not exist
Cotillion says the other side is unresolved and is where the three of them need to go, but can't explain because perception would affect their destination
Cotillion summons Shadowthrone, and they demand he explain better
Shadowthrone does not explain better
‘It is as Cotillion believes. The rooster died of grief’
Cotillion says supplies are waiting by the longhouse and that they're running out of time
Shurq Ellale’s crew sails on the Undying Gratitude along the coast of the Reach trying to escape a freezing storm, mountains of ice are moving towards the coast
First Mate Skorgen Kaban approaches Shurq wanting to return to Lether after not being chased anymore by the Edur
Shurq decides instead to head to Second Maiden Fort

cards.h: Scene 3 (Second Maiden Fort harbor, Shurq Elalle)

i.html: The Undying Gratitude sails away from the icebergs and ice sheets containing earth, tree roots, broken rocks that churned and sunk into the icy depths
Shurq thinks everything is piling up on Fent Reach and battering the Edur coast
The ship sails into the harbor of the Second Maiden Fort, a prison island where the inmates had mutinied and claimed independence
Toll-takers Pithy (short) and Brevity (tall) boarded the ship to inspect the cargo and charge 15 docks a day to anchor and 5 docks to land
Skorgen Kaban noticed a foreign dromon with black charred streaks, Shurq is surprised the ship survived such a powerful sorcerous attack
Brevity recognizes Skorgen Kaban “The Pretty” as he is famous and claims to have spent a lot of money on his lost eye, which a lot of people claim to have
Skorgen says his eye is a different color, heterochromatic which is bad luck for sailors
The icebergs and sheets break against the island, they are safe
Pithy says the ice sheets up north have simply broken off. For the past week the weather has very hot for the island which is uncommon
Shurq asks about the Edur, Brevity claims they fled when they saw the island’s fortifications and mages
Shurq is adamant about negotiating directly to the harbormaster, Shake Brullyg. Grand Master of the Putative Assembly
Shurq Elalle knew what crime Brullyg committed and is surprised to find a full-blooded Shake here
Pithy and Brevity return home
Udinaas watches Seren Pedac polish the Trull’s marriage proposal sword
The Onyx Wizards are chanting, Silchas Ruin is speaking to them
Andara was a blackstone edifice monastery at the bottom of a gorge, cliffs full of caves that led to dead ends, bridges over chasms, towers/spires,
The Amass was a lake of hardened lava streaked with red, the chamber the Bluerose Tiste Andii population would gather barefoot to watch the five Onyx Wizards argue
Reve Masters of Rock, Air, Root, Dark Water, and Night
The population was 500, only 14 were pure blood Tiste Andii besides the Reve Masters, only 3 people have seen daylight
They were insane
Udinaas jokes that Silchas and the Onyx Wizards were discussing how to execute the Tiste Edur in their presence, Fear

Makes fun that Fear is like a hero that entered the villain’s lair and describes an elaborate and sarcastic DnD campaign where the evil villain lures heroes by possessing a magic item that threatens a necromantic army
Heroes come in droves, one slaughters the minions and leaves, bringing a plague he caught to whatever city he retreats to which causes an epidemic, his name cursed by all
The hero’s followers become adopted by the villain to make more glorious items that lures more heroes into a trap
Ramble ends

Fear recalls the story among the women Edur that Scabandari Bloodeye had chosen to die, so that he could seek absolution on the Grey Road for his guilt [over his betrayal of Silchas and the Tiste Andii] on the Kechra (K’Chain) fields
Their mother Uruth told him the story, rejected the tradition of secrecy among the Edur women and wanted her sons to know
Fear believed Rhulad needed to grow and learn more before hearing the truth, but being in the shadow of his three older brothers made him impatient
Udinaas believes the Crippled God chose Rhulad over Hannan Mosag because he listened to what Rhulad had to say

The Crippled God recognized the perfection of the Tiste Edur’s history, politics, culture. Rhulad was the perfect victim of circumstance and in position to carry out The Crippled God’s plans, he had the right fatal flaws to exploit
Fear recognizes Udinaas’ value, says his intelligence and wisdom is wasted as a slave
Udinaas states is also the reason why slavery exists, or else too many people would rise up and challenge tyrants resulting in bloodbaths, which he’d rather not
The Onyx Wizards stop chanting
Clip watches as the Onyx Wizards end their debate and address Silchas Ruin

The Onyx Wizards wish to preserve balance, Silchas Ruin explains it was all because of Gothos’ sorcery of Omtose Phellack that froze the land. The ice is melting, the sorcery is failing, and the glaciers atop the mountain hold a spear aimed at the Andara

The Onyx Wizards assign Clip, revealed to be Anomander Rake’s Mortal Sword, to escort Silchas Ruin to the shadow of the “spear” to find Scabandari Bloodeye’s soul, warns that what he finds will be unexpected. Doing this will change the trajectory of the spear
Silchas Ruin is annoyed by Clip fidgeting with his chain, Clip doesn’t realize he’s doing it
Silchas Ruin returns to the ‘fell party’, pouring himself a glass of wine which he sorely appreciates after being buried for so long

Explains that Omtose Phellack sorcery prevented the Tiste Andii ghosts [Note: that died during Scabandari Bloodeye’s betrayal] from crossing through Hood’s Gate and thus are stuck on the mortal plane. Now they are with their mortal kin, the Bluerose Tiste Andii
Silchas has to clarify who Hood is because the god doesn’t exist on Lether
Silchas announces Clip as their new guide to find Scabandari Bloodeye’s soul
Fear expresses gratitude, that the Edur would be in Clip’s debt to find Father Shadow’s soul, Clip laughs
Silchas explains the Edur presents the biggest threat to the Tiste Andii, Fear says he’ll argue for everyone’s liberation
Seren doesn’t trust Clip
Atri-Preda Bivatt expresses her concern that overseer Brohl Handar is personally following her on Letur Anict’s mission to destroy the Awl [Note: in response to Redmask stealing livestock]
Brohl isn’t used to riding horses and does so awkwardly
Brohl says the Arapay clan of Tiste Edur faced much more dangerous foes than the Letherii and will be fine
He is reassured by his Arapay clan warriors and the K’risnan warlocks
Brohl asks why Bivatt met with Letur Anict
Bivatt tries to lie, saying it was for financial reasons. But the expedition is being entirely funded by the Edur’s money
Brohl knew Letur Anict is corrupt as hell, and knew his greedy ambitions were far too reckless even for the factor’s allies in the Chancellor, the Liberty Consign, and the Patriotists
[Note: Although the Edur controlled the empire, the Letherii were still the ones running the show. Isolating Rhulad from all other Edur while they continued to get rich. Brohl wants to end this]
Brohl finally feels confidence in his position as Overseer in the scheme of things
Atri-Preda Bivatt rides alongside Brohl Handar, frustrated because she actually likes him as a person
Flashes back to her conversation with factor Letur Anict, who predicted Brohl would impose himself on the mission and wants to use the opportunity to have him killed blame the Awl for it
Works under the false pretense that the Tiste Edur are conspiring against Emperor Rhulad, isolating Rhulad further
Bivatt excuses herself from Brohl’s side, finds a Bluerose horseman and whispers something to him
Toc-Anaster recovered well after Redmask convinced the Ganetok Awl clan to come to his side and killed the traitorous Hadralt, who baited the Grey Swords into being killed by the Letherii
However, Toc-Anaster is quite crazy and asks why the Awl children sing while putting beads on strings
Natarkas explains the song sets the order of the beads to tell a story, without words the story cannot be corrupted
Redmask explains how the Letherii twists the meanings of words to corrupt them, use them as weapons and deceive others
Toc-Anaster says ‘Togg’s teats’, and Redmask asks about the other Malazan curses
Togg’s teats, Togg is a male
Hood’s breath, Hood is dead and does not breathe
Beru’s mercy, the lord of storms has no mercy
Mowri fend, the lady of the poor fends off nothing
Redmask asks why worship those gods if they’re unhelpful, Toc-Anaster jokes how more unhelpful the gods would be if they didn’t
Redmask says how the wild wolves have eaten only the hearts of the dead Grey Swords
Redmask leads Toc-Anaster to a tent with a large map, a patchwork of smaller rodara-skin maps
Redmask wants Toc-Anaster to join as a soldier, but if Toc-Anaster wants to leave then Redmask will offer him supplies and wish him well
Toc-Anaster chooses to stay and tells Redmask about the Malazan army, helping Redmask turn the Awl into a professional army, and perhaps make a new song for the Awl to sing. A dirge.
Sukul Ankhadu waited in a glade for Sheltatha Lore to recover after finally being free from the Azath in Lether
Red hair, dried up skin like a T’lan Imass, bloodless flesh wounds, fingernails like beetles
Sheltatha Lore heard and felt Silchas Ruin’s memories as they were buried in the Azath
Believes Silchas Ruin anticipated Scabandari Bloodeye to betray him. His mind is draconean, his planning spans millennia
Sukul Ankhadu and Sheltatha Lore agree to work together against Menandore and Silchas Ruin
Taxilian sits down for wine with Samar Dev to share his perspective as an architect
Impressed by the causeways, bridges, canals, pumps, aqueducts, etc.
Unlike cities like Ehrlitan built on top of ancient ruins, the ancient city of Lether still retains the ancient patterns and gridwork it was first built on
Mystical nature regarding numbers, geometry, lattices of power that weaves energy through the city
Scale House collapsed when the Letherii returned with ‘champions’, the event may have had purpose
Taxilian warns Samar Dev to escape, but she knows Patriotists are always watching them
Samar Dev also feels loyalty to Karsa Orlong
Taxilian and Samar Dev leave to find the ruins of Scale House
Taralack Veed watches Icarium walk around a dusty compound looking at ancient friezes, damaged by warriors sparring
[Note: I imagine this is like those gladiatorial arena waiting rooms]
Taralack is hesitant about his place in the Nameless Ones schemes, people who worship the house [Azath] itself. Not its living occupants, not the builders, or not the god it’s supposed to honor
Taralack suggests Icarium to leave his weapon behind and explore the city
Icarium says he’s not ready yet. Icarium thinks Rhulad won’t start their fight yet because he’s scared
Taralack wonders if Icarium knows the history of Lether, and if the city has been waiting for him
Atri-Preda Yan Tovis sees her captain Varat Taun, a Bluerose Tiste Andii, curled up in a corner
Varat Taun is still traumatized from witnessing Icarium’s rage when the Tiste Edur tried to claim the First Throne of the T’lan Imass. Letherii healers can’t fix his broken mind
The Tiste Edur were upset that the Throne of Shadow was ‘destroyed’, and plans to send another expedition party to affirm its destruction
[Note: The Edur were fooled by Shadowthrone’s illusion, but all of the Tiste Edur witnesses are dead]
Senior Assessor, a Cabalhii monk comes at the request of Yan Tovis because no one else could heal Varat Taun
Senior Assessor volunteered to follow the Edur, the Cabal Archipelago’s way of appeasing foreign invaders with a hostage
Senior Assessor is his rank within the United Sects of Cabal
There are 3,012 sects of Cabal which all worship the One God. But because the One God didn’t write his tenets down, the other sects had religious and secular conflicts.
In the Great Synod of Year One, the sects united with each one having its own college and tenets
Senior Assessor is a Mocker, painting his face in a laughing expression, which the Mockers were forbidden to laugh
The One God helps no-one and is itself insane
Senior Assessor speaks fluid Letherii and can assess Yan Tovis’ social history and status by the way she speaks

Per the Mockers’ Doctrine, if people acquired ‘profound humility and respect for other people and the world they live in’ through achieving ‘clarity of thought and a cogent regard of morality’, then imbalance can be redressed and the One God will be sane once more
Senior Assessor uses High Mockra to heal the Cripple God’s corruption and High Denul to heal the brain physiologically
Senses the same false god that cursed Emperor Rhulad that damaged Varat Taun, the chaotic warrens
Varat Taun immediately recovers
When Varat Taun says he saw Icarium, Senior Assessor grabs his face, bites his lip until he bleeds, and runs away
Taralack Veed appears because he had a fear that Yan Tovis would try to stop Icarium from fighting Rhulad
Taralack and Varat have a moment together because of their shared trauma
[Note: By ‘taking his weight’ I’d like to imagine they hugged]
Yan Tovis plans to flee with Varat in two days, have him go home and be hired by the factor of Bluerose, possibly bring Senior Assessor
Taralack stays to carry out his duty and says Emperor Rhulad is only being used in a war among the gods
‘And take this brave warrior with you. Do this, and I will die empty of sorrow’

cards.h: Scene 5 (Temple of the Errant, the Errant)

i.html: The Temple of the Errant was a beehive dome central chamber at the end of a long corridor in an abandoned passage of the Old Palace, sealed behind massive cut limestone
The altar at the center was destroyed
The Errant had left the Temple 400 years ago, still heard whispers of his followers expressing their sense of betrayal
The Errant cried for his followers to show mercy for each other, they were enraged instead
The Forkrul Assail’s pogroms against his followers made the Errant weak
Fener, the Boar of War, hides in the Temple. He wants sanctuary in exchange for the Hold of the Beast that has been awakened
Treach was too weak to take the throne, now occupied by the Wolves of Winter
The Errant agrees to block all prayers calling upon Fener
Feather Witch is surprised by her casting of the tiles
Axe [Fulcra/Unaligned, Eres] is bound to Saviour [Brys Beddict] and Betrayer [the Errant] of the Empty Hold
Knuckles [Fulcra/Unaligned, Sechul Lath] and the White Crow [Fulcra/Unaligned, Silchas Ruin] circle the Ice Throne
Elder [?] of Beast Hold stands at the Portal [?] of the Azath Hold
Gate [Clip] of the Dragon and Blood-Drinker [Silchas Ruin] converge on the Watcher [Gothos] of the Empty Hold
[Note: Putting in names listed on the fandom wiki, I still dunno what they could mean so here you go]
Feather Witch picks up several tiles
Shapefinder, the Errant does not show his face
Fiery Dawn, Menandore
Feather Witch thought the Dragon Hold dead, yet it vied for dominance with the Empty Hold. The throne of the Ice Hold should also be dead
FW puts away the tiles under her bed, look at an old book, Compendium of the Gods, and puts that away
FW uses a tile she inscribed an intricate pattern ‘Capture’, to capture a ghost which turned out to be the late Ceda, Kuru Qan
While activating the tile, she sees the Tracker of the Beast Hold chase its quarry into a trap
Kuru Qan wonders what FW plans to do with Brys Beddict’s fingers and makes a bargain to wait for his aid before carrying out vengeance plans
Samar Dev and Taxilian visit the collapsed Scale House
Samar Dev senses lots of spirits, all of them rats, and feels far older than the d’ivers Gryllen
Samar Dev leaves knowing the Patriotists are always watching them
Bugg carried a sack of live chickens and meets Tehol in an alley
Tehol laments getting live chickens because now they have to actually kill them
The duo pass by the ruins of Scale House, Tehol remarks that the foreign witch [Note: Samar Dev] is gone, considers her handsome but would never voice such a backhanded compliment
The duo go home
Sirryn Kanar, a Patriotist Sergeant of the Guard, embodies all the values of fascism, misogyny, privilege, and ‘fear of what they do not understand’ that the Patriotists produces
Sirryn leads his men to kill a Tiste Edur guarding Nisall’s quarters, kicks the door down, and kills two handmaidens while arresting a third

cards.h: Scene 10 (Eternal Domicile, Bruthen Trana & Triban Gnol)

i.html: An hour passed after Sirryn Kanar’s raid, Bruthen Trana enters Nisall’s quarters with the Arapay warlock, K’ar Penath
Bruthen plans to take 16 Tiste Edur warriors and the warlock up to the Patriotist HQ to release the handmaiden
Chancellor Triban Gnol appears with two bodyguards, acknowledging the two dead women were innocent and puts the blame Nisall
Bruthen nearly strangles Triban and tosses him to the ground, Triban braces the fall with his hand and breaks his fingers, Bruthen walks away
Triban swears to have Bruthen dead and to get rid of his useless bodyguards, planning to strike out their families pensions and demand each of their eldest children as Indebted
Nisall
Nisall is thrown into a jail cell, Karos Invictad enters demanding a written confession as a traitor to the empire and accepts execution
Her handmaiden, Tissin, has already complied and has been decapitated
Karos takes Nisall to his office, Nisall sees Tehol and Bugg’s insect puzzle
Nisall writes on the vellum page and states she is pregnant with Emperor Rhulad’s heir
Karos Invictad leaves the room to fetch a healer
Commotion happens outside, Karos returns and stabs Nisall several times with his sword cane. Nisall dies ☠
Bruthen Trana
Bruthen Trana sees Karos stabbing Nisall, picks up Nisall’s ‘confession’, and beats Karos bloody and unconscious
K’ar Penath stops him from killing the invigilator
Bruthen orders to wrap up Nisall and Tissin to return to the Eternal Domicile
Tanal Yathvanar panics as he thinks Karos Invictad has taken Janath Anar away from him
He returns to the HQ as guards report to him of Bruthen Trana’s attack, Tanal wishes Karos was finished off instead of being left alive
Tanal finds Karos Invictad a bloody, pissy mess on the floor
Karos had called upon Tanal during Nisall’s arrest but Tanal wasn’t at home though he claimed to be
Tanal pours glasses of wine and asks how Karos got rid of the academic, realizing from his expression that he did not take Janath Anar
Bruthen Trana tells warlock K’ar Penath about how he plans to mobilize the Tiste Edur and Hannan Mosag to wage a civil war against the Letherii behind Rhulad’s back
Believes there was a reason that made the Patriotists panic and kill Nisall
Bruthen won’t go to Rhulad yet, plans to hide the bodies
K’ar Penath feels pride in witnessing Bruthen this night, happy to get out of this viper pit of a civilization and pledges to support him when he speaks to Hannan Mosag
Believes Triban Gnol and Karos Invictad are ‘two snakes in a barrel soaked in oil’, and Triban will be the spark when the chancellor reports to Rhulad
Bugg and Tehol watch from above as the chickens run around in the home, one catches on fire
Janath Anar wakes up wearing a small shirt, recognizing Tehol as he hides behind Bugg

Tehol was one of many lovestruck students, as perverted as he was Janath Anar is glad to be with them. His harmless infatuation reminds her of better days after Tanal Yathvanar was the complete opposite in his beatings and rapes, while yelling how he loved her
Bugg climbs down to find the burning chicken
Rautos Hivanar leads a meeting of the Liberty Consign of Merchants
Present are Uster Taran, Druz Thennict, Horul Rinnesect, and Barrakta Ilk
Rautos addresses two issues: the sabotage of the Letherii economy and the Patriotist’s murder of Nisall, the First Concubine
Rautos has made moves to distance the Liberty Consign from the Patriotists and started hiring another people

As the meetings went on, Rautos repeatedly wiped at his hands. For years, corpses [those that the Patriotists kill and dump in the river] would wash up in the waters around his estate, and his hands become stickier with residue
Epigraph, Creed of the Mockers. The Cabalhii appears to have had an incident about Icarium’s rage (Hedge)
Hedge sits on the ruins of an altar, one of many structures that descended from the sky
Hedge has walked across this realm, seeing giant skeletons of possible gods, with a wind companion goading him to abandon his flesh and turn to dust
Hedge finds a dragon skeleton, its ribcage shattered as if collapsed inward by blunt force, bones appearing as if melted into glass
Two more dragon skeletons past it
The wind asks among the fallen, who would outnumber the rest. Hedge knows the answer to be children, but does not show despair because all men and women have to kill the child in them
Hedge does not give into the wind’s voice, assumes it’s a god that needs any bit of worship so that it could draw power and attempt an escape. Hedge does not give in because he is a soldier
(Hedge)
Hedge finds a tracks in the mud, the wind voice helps him deduce its a T’lan Imass

(in Gardens of the Moon) Survived the Siege of Pale. Joined Whiskeyjack’s crew to dig and bury munitions under the roads of Darujhistan, shot a munition at the Jaghut Tyrant that did a lot of damage. Nearly detonated the munitions with Fiddler, but was stopped by Kalam who knew the enter city sits on top of gas chambers.

(in Memories of Ice) The remained of the Sgt. Whiskeyjack’s 9th Squad (Hedge, Mallet, Quick Ben, and Trotts) were attached to Sgt. Antsy’s 7th Squad (Picker, Blend, Detoran, Spindle). Hedge got into shenanigans to steal the wooden table they used to play rigged card games on from the war council. Had a hate-love relationship with Detoran. Participated in the Siege of Capustan. At the Siege of Coral, the sappers were flown in by quorl so Hedge can breach the corner tower for the Bridgeburners to enter. K’Chain Che’Malle appear and Hedge throws a cusser straight into the ground, sacrificing himself to save the Bridgeburners.
(in House of Chains) The Tanno Spiritwalker’s song, given to Fiddler, has ascended the Bridgeburners.
(in Bonehunters) Hedge visits Fiddler in his drug-induced dream while they were buried under Y’Ghatan, says the Bridgeburners didn’t cheat death.

When Ganoes Paran summons all of Raraku’s dead, he also summons the Bridgeburners including Hedge to help summon the Deragoth to defeat Dejim Nebrahl. Along with the Jaghut Ganah, the three of them use the Raraku Sea as a gate and arrive at Verdith’anath, the Bridge of Death and Jaghut mythical underworld. The realm was older than the Holds and beneath Hood’s realm outside his domain. Hedge wonders what the ascended Bridgeburners are marching towards. In the Nascent, the arrive at the five Deragoth statues (Karsa had released two at the Battle of Raraku). Hedge detonates munitions to free the Deragoth and continues to wander the Nascent.
Varat Taun rides with Yan Tovis, Senior Assessor, and the rest of their Letherii company fleeing east away from Icarium’s inevitable rage
Varat thinks about the rumors around Yan Tovis being a coward for surrendering Fent Reach without a fight. But he has seen her courage countless times before
Varat Taun thinks about how he has a shared experience surviving with Taralack Veed, feels guilty that he was left behind, and decides to return to Letheras. Senior Assessor also joins him
No word to be given to his family in Bluerose
Trull Sengar, Onrack, and Quick Ben rowed a boat for a day until they hit shallow water, then waded in knee deep water for half a day
The group stops when Trull uses his spear like a 10 foot pole and perceives they came to a sheer drop off
Trull believes they are on a concourse because of flat the silt layer is
Onrack remarks of a massive K’chain Che’Malle city-state on the southeastern peninsula of Stratem where the ritual wars were fought, when the Short Tails rebelled
Trull feels inadequate not knowing anything, Onrack is a puppy dog trying to cheer him up, recognizing him as Knight of Shadow
Was not chosen by Cotillion, possibly influenced by the Eres’al, or happened from his attempt to stop Icarium’s rage
Quick Ben fades away to find a gate, mentions the Shadow Realm is dying

‘Trull Sengar, should I join this water as dust, I do not think I would return. Oblivion would take me with the promise of a struggle ended. Not what I desire, friend, for that would mean abandoning you. Yet what does a warrior do when peace is won?’
‘Take up fishing,’ muttered Quick Ben
Quick Ben is frustrated at Shadowthrone for throwing Kalam, his lifelong friend, into an Azath, and wants to get him out
Spiritually, Quick Ben searched for a gate

Reaching out his awareness, pressed against a smooth surfaced that was pockmarked like a sponge until a sudden tear opened and pulled him into clouds until he stood on a soft ground of a tundra, a shallow valley with miniature trees and large dragonflies feeding on midge flies
Knowing this is their destination, Quick Ben wakes up with a cough, startling Trull
Ballant owns a tavern that’s served Second Maiden Fort since it was a prison island
There had been a group of foreigners that would spend time at Brullyg Shake’s palace then waste time playing games at the tavern
For several days he’d sit silently at Shurq Elalle’s table because he’s infatuated with her
Shurq thinks the earthy skinned person and a faint blue skinned person reminds her of people in Iron Bars’ squad
Ballant tells them about how they spend their time, Shurq figures they’re the ones that saved Second Maiden Fort from the ice storm and now Brullyg Shake is beholden to them
Shurq wants Ballant to let her crew deliver the cask of Fent ale he regular orders every three days

cards.h: Scene 7, 8 (Bluerose Mountains, Seren Pedac & Silchas Ruin)

i.html: (Seren Pedac)
Seren Pedac and friends have been traveling for four days north through the Bluerose mountains towards the sea
Large masses of ice have been melting and imperceptibly
[Note: Remnants of Gothos’ Omtose Phellack sorcery]
Fungi grows on the dead plants and animals that had been trapped for centuries, the spores Seren’s allergies to act up and sneeze
Seren mentions that she feels loss of purpose since Clip is now leading their group
Fear Sengar begs her not to leave, Seren asks why
Udinaas says its because Trull’s sword marriage proposal, tangent on words unsaid, and jests that Fear is the last honorable Sengar brother alive
Fear takes offense and grabs Udinaas’ shirt, tossing him to the floor
Seren tells Udinaas not to do that again if he values his life, Udinaas responds who in the party is not suicidal
Kettle pipes up that she doesn’t want to die, Udinaas’s smile breaks and turns into grief before he turns his head away
Seren Pedac says Trull is dead, the group continues hiking
(Silchas Ruin)
Clip asks Silchas Ruin what’s up with the rest of the party, gets bitter words in response
Clip mentions he has a lot of bastard kids in Bluerose
Toc-Anaster remembers his life as Toc the Younger, but feels cravings for human flesh as Anaster the Tenescowri
Rides along with the x14,000 Awl warriors, ~x7,000 Awl non-warriors, x20,000 rodara livestock, x3,000 herd dogs, and dray wolf-hunters
Wonders how Redmask was able to get two alive K’Chain Che’Malle as his guards, and how he knew their names
Redmask has x20 myrid animal carcasses hollowed of their insides, filled with boiled potatoes, wrapped in hide and placed on wagons kept away from the other wagons

The Grey Swords had been cut to pieces. Slaughtered. Oh, they yielded their lives in blood enough to pay the Hound’s Toll, as the Gadrobi were wont to say. But what had their deaths meant? Nothing. A waste. Yet here he rode, in the company of his betrayers.
A Renfayar Awl clan elder rides next to Redmask, Sag’Churok, and Gunth Mach
The Renfayar elder senses that Toc Anaster dreams of running with wolves and that he should be killed, regardless that the Awl owe him
The Renfayar elder knows Redmask’s secret about his sister, taunting him yet wishing him victory for the Awl
Redmask does nothing in response
Stayandi was a Letherii girl whose brother was Abasard. Their family was indebted to factor Letur Anict and left the city life to become rodara shepherds on Awl land the factor owned
Two months before leaving the city, Stayandi was being punished by a mistress training her as a handmaiden. She was locked in a trunk lid, screamed until she lost her voice becoming mute
The land was magical because it was healing to her family. Emotionally, mentally, and physically
The magic land ended when Redmask killed Abasard and her family to reclaim the rodara for the Awl
[Note: Events of Chapter 4]
Stayandi ran away and was raised by wolves, crawling on all fours like them becoming a feral child
Stayandi woke up one morning alone, the wolves had left, and a dark tan man with a skeleton painted along his body and skull painted on his face
Looking at him, Stayandi remembers that she is human and followed the man
(Toc Anaster)
Toc Anaster kept watch to the north and saw nothing, Torrent (a young Awl warrior with red face paint) kept watch to the south and saw tracks of a dozen men on foot following an antelope track
Redmask plans to meet the possible Letherii three leagues away at the Bast Fulmar valley
Toc Anaster is a soldier, but the most he can do is stay with the elders and children
Redmask orders Torrent to also stay and train the children near their death nights, to Torrent’s dismay
Torrent tries to push the job onto Toc Anaster, Toc reminds him that he was the one that abandoned the Grey Swords alongside the dishonorable Hadralt
Toc doesn’t feel like he fits in as a soldier, both here and with the Malazans
A group of children run away from a muddy toddler trying to keep up, the toddler stops and cries
Toc makes a rude sound (read farting noise) and makes the toddler laugh
(Redmask)
Redmask is questioned by Natarkas about sending Torrent away, he believes it will make him wiser
Natarkas also wonders if it is worth it to surrender tradition and fight in an unhonorable way
Redmask says the traditions will not but fail, it is his war and he will win
Old Hunch Arbat stopped gathering excrement and piss from his neighbors to bury the Seregahl statues after the Tarthenal gods were killed [Note: by Iron Bars, Corlo, Silchas Ruin, and Ublala Pung]
His tarthenal neighbors were pissed, oen neighbor Vrager even kept pissing on his front door
Arbat was ready to leave his village behind until a Dream Mask of a terrifying power with cracks appeared in his dreams
Arbat woke up at evening and set his house on fire
The local Factor was leading a mob to check up on Arbat, the Factor is glad he’s alive
Tiste Edur troops are staying at the inn insisted the Tarthenal townsfolk go investigate, the Factor wonders if Vrager set the fire
Arbat lets the blame fall on Vrager, but insists the fire won’t spread to the woods because it’s raining, his home is cleared out on all side, and the puddles are basically a moat
Arbat doesn’t launch a formal complaint since Vrager has a cousin in Letheras and walks off
On the road, Arbat encounters Atri-Preda Yan Tovis who is unaware of the Edur troop staying in Arbat’s village
Yan Tovis asks if there’s anywhere private her troops can camp, Arbat suggests an abandoned homestead and barn

[Note: The homestead belonged to a horse breeder slaughtered by Letherii deserters during the Edur invasion. Seren Pedac and the Crimson Guard took horses from here and later came across the Seregahl statues]
Yan Tovis thanks him and Arbat continues walking off
Tehol lays on his belly as his look down at a scene worthy of a renaissance painting
Ten hens walking and clucking around, Ublala Pung pacing back and forth, Janath Anar making a pillow from chicken feathers, and Bugg stirring a pot of chicken soup with a chicken leg
Tehol climbs down the ladder flashing everyone below
Ublala accidentally steps on and kills a chicken, goes outside to relieve himself, and comes back in after eating a comfrey bush
Janath asks Bugg about his healing, concerned that she feels nothing despite retaining all of bad memories
Bugg says it’s not magic, it’s her own mind trying to protect itself. And also feeling attracted to Tehol
Ubalala has decided that he needs to take Tehol to meet and talk to the Toblakai champion, Karsa Orlong
Ormly, the champion rat catcher, had a meal with chief investigator Rucket
Scale House’s collapse was anticipated by the Rat Catcher’s Guild
Ormly is concerned that the Patriotists will become active with the Liberty Consign’s full support and funding
Rucket has sent rats to all the crypts in Lether and all other cities. They’re all empty
Tehol alleges that he can dump all of Lether’s coin back onto the streets at a moment’s notice if the Liberty Consign mints more coins
Ormly wants to take advantage of the tension between the Edur against the Patriotists and the Chancellor
Unn, the Tarthenal that murdered Gerun Eberict, fetches wine when Rucket asks
Hannan Mosag had enslaved a demon spirit-god during the conquest of the Letherii Empire
When they arrived at Lether, the demon spirit-god sensed a heart lower with enough potency to grant its freedom from Hannan Mosag
It was a trap by Ceda Kuru Qan, Mael/Bugg, and a Jaghut Huntress to encase the demon spirit-god in ice
The Errant looks at the frozen lake containing the demon spirit-god, wondered why Mael who was indifferent acted and took sides now
Mael gets power from his worshippers who abuse his indifference and spills blood in his name [Note: the Jhistal, Mallick Rel]
The Errant finds Feather Witch in a secret chamber
The ghost of Kuru Qan, the former Ceda, appears and warns that being near the demon spirit-god has afflicted the Errant with its ambition, lust, and desperation
The Errant wants his power back as Master of the Tiles, to resurrect the Elder Gods, to war against the warrens and the Master of the Deck
Kuru Qan warns that this is what the Crippled God wants
The Errant takes Feather Witch and cuts her, spilling mortal blood as Feather Witch stabs the Errant in the left eye with Brys Beddict’s finger
The Errant tosses her aside, but she tackles him until she gouges out his eye
The Errant walks away

cards.h: Scene 5, 6, 7, 8 (Settle Lake & the Cedance, Feather Witch & the Errant)

i.html: (Feather Witch)
Feather Witch holds Brys Beddict’s finger and the Errant’s left eye as she drags herself to the far wall of Settle Lake, demands Kuru Qan ghost to bring a healer
(The Errant)
The Errant throws the knife into the Errant tile at the center of the Cedance, the other tiles spin around it with Feather Witch’s blood filling the channels in between
Senses Hannan Mosag had been here
The Errant leaves to kill Feather Witch and make sure she doesn’t become his High Priestess
(Feather Witch)
As Feather Witch bleeds out and chokes on her blood, she swallows the Errant’s eye
(The Errant)
The Errant feels power taken from his heart and hears Feather Witch’s voice
Feather Witch has become the Errant’s Destrai Anant of the Empty Throne. God’s Chosen. The Well of Spirits.
Holds Brys Beddict’s finger and demands that he be healed and become the Errant’s Mortal Sword
Nominates Udinaas as the Errant’s Shield Anvil. T’orrud Segul, in the First Empire language.
FW says the Cedance now depicts the warrens, making the truth of things.
Oponn appears and is playing the game
The Errant silences her voice, believes he’s made a big mistake, and starts planning
Samar Dev watches as Karsa grabs a Meckros shield warrior, Gadalanak, and tosses him in the air
The other champions complain that Karsa fights like an animal, not at all good practice to fight Rhulad
Puddy makes boasts
Everyone looks at the Seguleh woman to step up to Karsa but she does nothing

Samar wonders about the Seguleh, a First Empire word meaning the Anvil. Wonders if they were a remnant clan or fragment army that settled on a faraway island colony. Her mask and glyphs were not from the First Empire though
Samar and Karsa feel trembling [Note: From the Errant claiming the Cedance and Empty Throne]
Samar goes back to her room and does a sealing ritual
Kuru Qan appears and begs her to heal Feather Witch
Samar refuses because FW gives witches a bad name
Instead, Samar Dev spits on her knife and stabs the ghost, trapping Kuru Qan in her blade
Karsa slams Samar Dev’s door open and walks through her magic wards like nothing. She claims only gods can do that
Karsa asks why Samar has imprisoned a ghost, when she used to bargain with them. It is unlike her

Samar says that she changed because being around Karsa is dangerous, that he can be immune to the universe’s influence through sheer will and ignorance, challenging her entire life’s world view. Everything about him scares her
Karsa flirts back, everything about him fascinates her too
Karsa leaves, answering the Seguleh woman’s challenge. Samar can’t help but chase after him

cards.h: Scene 11, 12, 13, 14 (Compound, Samar Dev and Taralack Veed)

i.html: (Samar Dev)
Samar Dev sees the Seguleh woman at the center of the practice area. Shoulder length greased hair and midnight eyes tracking Karsa through her mask, dual wielding thin-bladed longswords
Taralack Veed, Icarium, and Tomad Sengar are in the audience
(Samar Dev)
Karsa and the Seguleh woman swing at each other
Karsa ground stomps causing a tiny quake, disrupting the Seguleh’s flow for a fraction of a second enough for Karsa to swing his flint sword
The Seguleh breaks both her wrists trying to block. Attempts to kick Karsa’s crotch, but Karsa drops his sword to grab both her legs and lifts her up, dangling
(Taralack Veed)
Icarium faintly remembers dueling Karsa before, but was interrupted
Taralack is relieved when Icarium doesn’t want to resume the duel
(Samar Dev)
Samar speaks with Tomad Sengar
It’s decided that Karsa Orlong will be last, everyone else is entertainment
Karsa walks up to Samar, thinking Icarium had fled because Mappo isn’t there to interrupt their duel
Samar rejects Karsa’s attempt to sleep with her
Hannan Mosag calls out Mother Dark and Father Shadow to make an alliance between Andii, Liosan, and Edur and bring their children together
Reveals he wanted to take the Throne of Shadow and use the Crippled God’s chains to pull together the fragments of Kurald Emurlahn together and heal the land
With no response, Hannan Mosag’s accepts a Letherii as Mortal Sword of Emurlahn
Hannan Mosag wakes to find Bruthen Trana before him
The K’risnan K’ar Penath had spoken highly of Bruthen, Hannan sees the man as loyal Tiste Edur before Rhulad’s rule
Hannan tasks Bruthen to travel west and finds someone who is ‘dead, but not dead. Whose tomb has always been empty. Never spoken of but always present’
Hannan can’t speak plainly because of the Crippled God’s power in his body
Must get an item from Feather Witch
Tehol teaches Ublala Pung how to skulk as they make their way closer to the champions’ compound for Ublala to speak to the Tarthenal, Karsa Orlong
The duo crosses the bridge over the Quillas Canal, pass the Tolls Repository, and get spotted near the Eternal Domicile
Ublala wanted to create a diversion as he did with Shurq Elalle, except make Tehol the diversion as Ublala finds Karsa

cards.h: Scene 18, 19 (Eternal Domicile, Bruthen Trana & Feather Witch)

i.html: (Bruthen Trana)
Bruthen Trana thinks about how he doesn’t trust Hannan Mosag, but agrees to work with him
Wants to free the Letherii slaves unjustly imprisoned so together they can oppose the Patriotists and kill Karos Invictad
However, Bruthen must leave to find their savior whom he believes is under the ocean
He goes to find the slave, Feather Witch
(Feather Witch)

Feather Witch is frightened as Bruthen picks her up by her hair, pulls the necklace containing Brys Beddict’s finger until the cord painfully snaps against her neck, and throws her head against the wall
Tehol comes home without Ublala, the whole city is in alarm. Janath Anar and Bugg drink ‘hen tea’
Bugg thinks Ublala wants to speak to Karsa Orlong to see if he is a new god, or an ascendant
Samar Dev is woken up by Ublala knocking on her door after killing two guards
She leads him to Karsa, Ublala kneels before him, and Karsa punches Ublala because Toblakai kneel to no one
Ublala says ‘Lead us, Warleader’
The rest of the Tarthenal have been defeated by Letherii sorcery, the legends say they’ve been scattered by ice and betrayal. Similar to Karsa’s slave tattoos
Mentions Arbanat, a Tarthenal shaman who was not powerful enough to stop the Letherii
[Note: Probably Old Hunch Arbat]
Karsa tasks Ublala Pung gather the Tarthenal hiding on the Draconean Sea islands and bring them back to be Karsa’s army
Atri-Preda Bivatt and Brohl Handar lead their forces and have found the Awl campfires
Bivatt plans to engage them at Bast Fulmar Valley, she does not want to let the Edur fight, only her Letherii
Bivatt believes the battle will be bloody, but a decisive for the Letherii believing the Awl will lose as they always have done
The young Awl warrior Torrent insults and is dismissive of Toc Anaster for crafting stone-headed arrows as Tool had taught him
The Awl campfires is a ruse that successfully tricked the Letherii army as Redmask plans the attack
The Renfayar elder comes sending sorcery on the arrows and that he doesn’t trust Toc
Toc and the elder exchange secrets in some sort of one-up contest
The Renfayar elder claims he saw
Redmask’s sister kill herself
thousands of canoes on the north shore
skeletons run on the plains they’re in
knows the truth of Bast Fulmar
that their victory in the past was actually a loss
that Redmask will betray them
Toc Anaster responds about his life as Toc and Anaster’s Tenescowri cannibal body
The Renfayar elder waves his hands and banished Toc from the Awl wards
Toc hears a howl of a wolf
Toc asks Torrent, who has been eavesdropping nearby, if Redmask can bully the Awl into honor
Hedge follows the trail and finds Emroth, a Kron T’lan Imass
Born in the ‘Season of Blood-from-the-Mountain’, Eptr clan. They arrived at Jagra Til
She wielded a flint scimitar with an antler hilt, and half her face was shattered
Hedge talks about how his ears are too big and his knees are too knobby, unattractive to women which is why he never found love
Talks about how Detoran ‘loved’ him, but was even more unattractive and inarticulate (not unintelligent) with words than hewas
When they died, Hedge and Detoran worked it out in the afterlife more or less
Emroth responds how she understands why he has no companions, talking so much
Emroth feels he’s trying to get her to speak about her past and won’t be fooled
Hedge responds she probably doesn’t even remember her past because the T’lan Imass sacrificed themselves for their vengeance against the Jaghut.
The Imass made themselves the first victims
The irony is that the Jaghut weren’t that evil or dangerous at all and fought amongst themselves enough
The Jaghut used ice magic, but the Imass made their hearts even colder and lifeless
Emroth responds that she is Unbound, still has all her memories, and the memories that broke her are of love
The two continue walking in silence until they reach Omtose Phellack ice, a ridge with the silhouette of building tops. Emroth believes her home is on the other side
(In House of Chains)

Aramala and Cynnigig are Jaghut that fought alongside the T’lan Imass to defeat Jaghut Tyrants. After, the Imass had betrayed the Jaghut committed to their genocide. A group of 8 T’lan Imass scouts had found Aramala in her tower, Aramala killed seven of them while the eighth scout fled and returned with an T’lan Imass army who pinned her with a rock and sealed her with Tellann. The seven scouts that died were entombed in darkness for their failure.

Overtime, they became worshiped by the Teblor as the Seven Faces in the Rock. The Seven had sworn fealty to the Crippled God in exchange for breaking the Vow Ritual of Tellann and became the Unbound. They had cultivated their Teblor worshipers and ultimately led to following Karsa Orlong as spirits. Following him onto the Silanda to a dreamworld within barrow mounds that leads to the realm of Omtose Phellack.

Karsa follows the trail of the T’lan Imass army and exits the Omtose Phellack Warren into the Jaghut Odhan. Here, Karsa finds a flint quarry containing a network of caves holding a cache of Imass flint weapons. The Unbound arriving to their cache of weapons was the last task to free them from the Vow. The Unbound aid Karsa in making his own flint sword and imbuing it with the Ritual of Tellann to make it indestructible. Karsa was offered to be the eighth member of the Unbound, the souls of sacrificed Teblor children as his army, and the position of Knight of Chains. Instead Karsa destroys Sinballe and tells them to fuck off, never touch the Teblor again. Karsa grants Sinballe oblivion by throwing her skull into the ocean.

(in the Bonehunters) Five of the Unbound came to Barathol Mekhar’s village at the Tapur Crossroads. Months later Heboric, Greyfrog, Scillara, Crokus, and Felisin Younger came to the village. The Unbound attacked them and kidnapped Felisin Younger to bring to the city of the fallen, Hanar Ara. Kulat, a seneschal of the Crippled God, has prepared the city for her and proclaimed her Sha’ik Reborn. Those broken and crippled by Poliel’s plague came to populate the city. However, Felisin the Younger disbands the Rebel army and abandons the Book of Dryjhna to start a new book of Salvation.
Urual, Mossy Bone
Sin’b’alle, Lichen for Moss
Found oblivion when Karsa threw her skull into the Raraku sea.
Ber’ok, Dead Ash Tree
Haran’alle, Antler from Summer
Thek Ist, Spear Leg
Emroth, Fanged Skeleton
Currently with Hedge
Kahlb, Red Moss
Udinaas dreams of a battered stone temple atop a barren hill surrounded by thousands of Forkrul Assail corpses. His own body crippled
The Errant, covered in blood, steps out from the temple. He screams into the air, then does a Darth Vader force choke and drags Udinaas towards him
Menandore, in her golden-scaled dragon form, appears with ‘lighting without fire, thunder with no sound’ shaking the sky
Argent flames emanating from her scales burn the Forkrul Assail bodies, popping blisters and melting the fat of their bodies
The Errant wants Udinaas as his T’orrud Segal (Shield Anvil) so he can save the Forkrul Assail
Menandore says he’s the one that killed the Forkrul Assail, claims Udinaas because he is the father of their child
[Note: Rud Elalle of the Refugium raised among Imass]
They agree to an exchange, the Errant will nudge her sisters Sukul Ankadu and Sheltatha Lore out of Menandore’s way and he can have Udinaas
The Errant also tells her that their child is grown and is his own person
Udinaas stands up to his rapist, claims that he was the one that summoned them into his dream
Udinaas wakes into another fever dream that he caught from the rotting ice while hiking the Bluerose Mountains
Kettle saw his dream, says the stone temple fell over because it couldn’t handle the grief of all those souls
Udinaas will do what the Errant wants, but not in the way the Errant thinks it will happen
Kettle warns Udinaas not to cry too soon, he has to wait
Udinaas goes back to dreams he can control, of feasts
Seren Pedac wakes with the morning sun. Fear struggles to ignite frozen wood, Kettle offers some grass
Udinaas wakes up with a dry laugh and says some possibly foreshadowing thoughts
Silchas Ruin might turn into a dragon
Kettle opens her mouth like a door, Fear falls into it devoured by his own hunger to betray
Seren will conjure lost histories
Clip will sink his hands in blood and try to manipulate events
Silchas believes necromantic K’Chain Che’Malle sorcery released from the melting ice is causing Udinaas’ fever
Seren takes a knife to dig out clean pieces of ice to melt for drinking water and tosses in a pot
She channels Erikson’s archeological skills in studying the rotted flesh and detritus revealed from the melting ice
Using her weight to dig out ice, an entire slab lifts revealing a T’lan Imass spear underneath
Polished amber colored. Successive, intricate layering of horn gave it a mottled appearance. The spear head was ground jade, milky smooth, and leaf shaped.

[Possible Spoilers: The Imass spear seems like it’s going to be important, but after going through the book and seeing where else it can pop up.. I don’t think it’s important. I don’t think it’s the same spear that the Black Onyx Wizards claim is pointed at Andara.]
Clip walks up to Seren, curious about her findings
For some reason in response to weapons he does or does not use, he says he doesn’t hide in trees or throws fruit because he was born in Darkness
Emphasizes that he was born in Darkness tens of thousands of years ago, blessed by Mother Dark who turned away from the Tiste Andii
Clip claims he can walk the Darkness, and that Silchas Ruin cannot
Insinuates that Udinaas and Seren are threats to Silchas, that keeping this secret from Silchas will keep them alive
Also claims the T’lan Imass spear belongs with them [Note: Not sure if referring to the party itself, or the Tiste Andii]
Seren brings back the spear for Udinaas to use as a crutch
Silchas remarks that the spear does not belong to him and needs to be surrendered eventually
Later after hiking through a region with no trees only lichen and moss, the party takes a soup break
Udinaas says the spear slides like grease in his hands and can’t fight with it even if he wanted to
Clip says spears are easy, though he’s yet to meet a spearman he couldn’t beat
Fear and Seren laugh, thinking about Trull and his skill with the spear
Silchas kills the mood and tells everyone to keep moving
Quick Ben continues walking with Trull Sengar and Onrack, thinking about all the people he’s lost ever since the Siege of Pale
The N’purel catfish surround the group until a large one swims towards them
Trull notices that fighting Icarium made Quick Ben weakened on a deeper level, Onrack is more than willing to sacrifice himself and be left behind if QB isn’t strong enough to summon a gate
Quick Ben assures it more has to do with their destination and forces a gate open
The party goes through the gate into an open tundra of Tellann
Onrack becomes flesh and blood. Heavy brow, wind burnished skin, green eyes beneath epicanthic folds, a nose that’s broad, flat, and appeared to have been broken several times
Trull falls to his knees and cries
Masarch and the rest of the Awl listen to Redmask tell the story of Bast Fulmar, as he is flanked by Gunth Mach and Sag’Churok
Bast Fulmar, the Valley of Drums, was believed by the Letherii to be a historical site of battle between the Awl and K’Chain Che’Malle
The truth, it is the site where Shamans of the Antler cast magic that killed the land so they could leave and wage war
Bast Fulmar may be the site of the Tellann Ritual, where Imass gathered to become T’lan Imass
Magic is dead in Bast Fulmar, Redmask plans to take advantage of this against the Letherii
Atri-Preda Yan Tovis arrives at Boaral Keep, 30 leagues of the port town Rennis
The origin of the Grass Jackets Brigade. The current Dresh-Preda is a distant relative to the Boaral family
Yan Tovis enters the keep and meets Pully and Skwish
The women say Boaral Dresh had murdered his wife and Yan Tovis sends for a rider to acquire a Letherii adjudicator to pass judgment on the him
From their taloned feet, Yan Tovis deduces that the old women were among the 200 Shake witches and warlocks
They reveal they cursed the Boaral family for murdering the Shake in the past by driving all the men insane and killing their wives
Yan Tovis demands the witches to end the curse, using her authority as the Twilight, Shake Princess
The Shake witches bow their heads and reveal that her Queen mother was killed by the demon spirit-god [Hannan Mosag] had controlled to conquer Letheras
Yan Tovis is saddened by the news despite not seeing her mother in over a decade
The Shake witches also reveal Yan Tovis is to be betrothed to Shake Brullyg of Second Maiden Fort, but they don’t know if he remains there because the shore is blind to the sea for almost a month
They are unable to seek or communicate beyond the waves, ice and dark whisperings
Yan Tovis decides to go retrieve the Master of Arms who went to investigate a mystery of disappearing fishermen and dark voices from the sea
The Master of Arms is Yedan Derryg, aka the Watch [Shake title, I’m guessing like a guardian of the Shore]
Half-brother to Yan Tovis who also fled the responsibility of being royal-blooded Shake, the two never met before
In Midnight Tides, she had a small appearance. She was Atri-Preda at Fent Reach, had bloodlessly surrendered to the invading Tiste Edur

In Bonehunters, she was assigned to Preda Tomad Sengar’s 3rd Imperial Fleet to harass the north coast of Seven Cities to find challengers to Rhulad, liberate subjugated Edur tribes like Sepik, and massacre their oppressors. Taralack Veed had to convince Yan Tovis that Icarium is a worthy challenger. She was present when Tomad’s fleet attacked the Malaz 14th Army fleet and he recognized the Edur ship Silanda
Hound Master Bellict weeps as his wardogs were all dying from eating poisoned meat left on the ground by the Awl
16,000 Letherii and 2,000 Tiste Edur

Bivatt planned marched for two hours to reach the valley at dawn, expecting the Awl at midday from their fake camp location at the east side and negate their sun rise advantage (the sun rises in the east)
However the Awl are already half a league away, now the Letherii were at the disadvantage facing the sun rise
Blamed the Edur’s K’risnan warlocks for being lazy
Letherii doctrine to avoid sending outriders vulnerable to Awl raids and ambushes
The Awl side
At the valley far side, horse-archers were riding back and to create a dust cloud in front of the south broad slope. The dust cloud blocked vision of what’s beyond the ridges
On the north side, five Awl wedges wielding spears instead of sabotaged Letherii swords sold by the factor’s agents
Brohl Handar is concerned about the drainage channels in the Bast Fulmar valley
The narrow channels divided the battlefield into segments
All three channels on the Letherii side are on the south
On the Awl side there are one on the north, two in the middle, and one on the south
The north channel narrows. The Dresh ballista placed the bluff can’t be targeted from that side
Bivatt wants to use the southern flanks to push the Awl towards the north choke point where the Dresh ballistas will mow them down
Bivatt is unwilling to listen to any Brohl Handar about how Redmask can poke holes in her plan
Bivatt believes they cannot retreat, behind them are plains leaving the Letherii vulnerable to skirmishes, feints, and raids from the Awl’s superior horse warriors and war dogs
Brohl reveals that the K’risnan believe magic is dead in the Bast Fulmar Valley, on the plains at least they will be able to use magic
Bivatt commits to fighting in the valley
The medium infantry in reserve protects Letherii mages that will protect a feigned retreat if necessary
Bivatt recounts the Letherii position as she stands in the center of the Letherii west side facing east
South, widest approach for the Awl. The Bluerose lancers would charge and the Crimson Rampant shield-wall would push the Awl northward
Closest to Bivatt.
1500 medium infantry, Drene Garrison
At the top of the slope.
1500 medium infantry, Crimson Rampant Brigade in shield wall formation
Flanked by 500 heavy infantry, Harridict Brigade
Farthest from Bivatt.
1000 skirmishing light infantry, Crimson Rampant
1500 skirmishing Artisan Battalion
1500 Bluerose lancers
Center. Would swing either north or south depending on the state of the battle
1000 heavy infantry, Merchant’s Battalion in sawtooth formation
North.
Closest to Bivatt
~750 heavy infantry, Artisan Battalion
1000 skirmishers, Harridict Brigade
Farther from Bivatt
1,000 heavy infantry, Crimson Rampant Brigade in sawtooth formation. Bivatt’s ‘mailed fist’
Bluerose lancers intending to feint and instead ride around the Dresh ballistae and into the riverbed beyond the chokepoint
Farthest from Bivatt
Medium infantry, Crimson Rampant Brigade in shield wall formation to guard the ‘mailed fist’
Bivatt begins to motion her units
North Crimson Rampant heavies (mailed fist) to advance halfway
North Bluerose lancers to round the north chokepoint
Both sides, skirmishes marched down to the river bed
South Bluerose lancers lead to the edge of the riverbed, Crimson Rampant mediums and Harridict heavies follow
The Battle of Bast Fulmar begins
Awl light skirmishers engage with slingers, archers, javelins, hide shield and scimitars
The horse-archers disappeared, then reappeared and fired at the Letherii skirmishers
The Awl skirmishers retreat when the Harridict heavies arrive, tossing their hide shields & scimitars away
Awl horse-archers advanced in a line, the Letherii skirmishers retreated
The horse-archers wheel and form a line, firing at the Letherii skirmishers’ flanks and mow them down
The horse-archers rotate their line formation as they fire against the Harridict heavies, Crimson Rampant mediums, and Bluerose lancers
The horse-archers then immediately retreat as the Letherii advance
Awl heavy horse-warriors advance, outnumbering the Bluerose lancers 2:1
The Bluerose lancers wheel to meet the Awl heavies and are slaughtered
Bivatt advanced the Letherii mediums and heavies
The Awl light skirmishers (that abandoned their hide shields and scimitars) returned with rectangular copper shields and long spears
The north Bluerose lancers rounding to the chokepoint and Dresh ballistae were attacked by Awl wardogs
The Awl skirmisher wedges were spaced apart to make lanes wide enough for six wheeled wagons to be pushed and roll into the Crimson Rampant “mailed fist”
In the wagon beds were half naked warriors formed a half turtle shell with their spears sticking out
Once crashed, they jumped out and attacked the Crimson Rampant
Bivatt sounds the retreat as the Letherii baggage camps are being attacked
Brohl Handar waited with the 2,000 Edur warriors, 8 Arapay clan leaders, four warlocks, and a K’risnan of the Den-Ratha Edur clan
Brohl orders to send two cohorts to the camp, believing if Bivatt calls for reinforcements then they already lost
The K’risnan senses the rumbling of a huge monster
Awl warriors and the K’Chain Che’Malle attack
Brohl recognizes them as the Edur’s ancient enemy
Sag’Churok (male K’ell Hunter) bit chunks off several horses, sliced at several Edur with their blade arms, crushed horses and Edur under their taloned feets
Brohl’s horse collided with something and he was tossed over the horse’s head, his own scimitar slicing open his thigh as he fell and rolled on the ground
A K’risnan blasted Sag’Churok with sorcery to no effect and was crushed under its feet
Brohl’s blood gushes from his femoral artery being cut open
Bivatt watches as Gunth Mach (female drone, no blade arms) tears into the medium reserves to rip apart the Letherii mages with her hands and flees
Bivatt sounds the retreat back to camp and sees that Redmask is not pursuing
Two hours before sunrise, Yan Tovis rode with three riders in the dark to find Yedan Derryg
Yan Tovis thinks about her people, the Shake
The Shake believes the world started as nothing but sea, and inevitably the sea will rise and devour all
The Shake witnessed from their homeland, the Isle (transformed into the prison island Second Maiden Fort). The shore was their metaphor of land vs. sea
The Isle used to be connected to the main lands with land bridges, all have sunken now
Some Shake newborns were born grotesque with monstrous features
Taloned hands and feet, scaled elongated face, a tail, and lurid green eyes
The coven of Shake Witches would choose some, the rest of the children would be sacrificed to the sea

Something very strange and not further explained, demons engaged in war concerned about their species’ survival dumped their seed into the ocean which ends up washing onto shore, clinging on any living thing, maybe even hijacking a baby in the womb giving the Shake babies the demonic features
Yan Tovis left the Shake because of the sacrificing of babies too demonic, the witches and warlocks having controlled the Shake taking power, and belief from the Shore
The Shake people were viewed with disgust by the Nerek, Tarthenal, Faered, and Letherii
Yan Tovis had chosen each person in her company because of their Shake ancestry, however diluted it may be
Yan Tovis rides to the shore and meets Yedan Derryg
Yedan Derryg was a bearded man wearing black chain hauberks and a single bladed axe. His three Shake soldiers wielded lances

Yedan Derryg recognizes Yan Tovis from when she was a child, and receives a report about the situation at the Keep. Dresh Boaral is dead, and Tiste Edur from Rennis had been called to investigate an already solved murder
Yedan Derryg felt that he was summoned to the shore. The air had been still, but now it rains for the first time.
The horizon glows from burning Malazan ships slowly approaching
Yan Tovis believes the Malazan has come to punish the Letherii for the murder of Malazan subjects
They are here. On this shore. The Malazans are on our shore.
